profile.locationBio: McGuireWoods traces its origins to 1834 and has grown into a U.S.-based international law firm with a broad practice built around business clients. The firm serves companies and institutions across corporate and finance matters, mergers and acquisitions, banking regulation, private equity, labor and employment, intellectual property, tax, and private wealth services. McGuireWoods also maintains substantial capabilities in disputes and investigations, including antitrust, healthcare litigation and enforcement, data privacy and cybersecurity, securities matters, government investigations, restructuring, and energy-related counseling and litigation.

Founded in 1926 by Pio Bozzi and John Ganzi in New York City, The Palm began as an Italian restaurant and soon shifted into a steakhouse after a customer requested steak, setting the tone for a dining format built around classic service and hearty fare. The Palm's menu and identity have centered on prime beef, lobster, surf and turf, and traditional Italian dishes, while the restaurants have also served as gathering places for business meals, family celebrations, and social occasions. Over time, The Palm expanded from a single restaurant into a broader chain across the United States and into Mexico City, preserving a long-running tradition of welcoming service and a familiar, family-style atmosphere.

Palisades Ventures is a Los Angeles-based VC fund making growth stage investments in systems, services, software, and hardware companies that are driving the adoption of leading edge Information Technology, communications, and media technologies.

UBS began in 1998 through the merger of Union Bank of Switzerland and Swiss Bank Corporation, while the firm's roots go back to 1862. The company provides wealth management, asset management, investment banking, and banking services for private, corporate, intermediary, and institutional clients. The company maintains a broad international presence and offers financial services across many markets, with banking in Switzerland and a wider platform for clients around the world. The company uses the UBS brand name that came from Union Bank of Switzerland.

Hyperdynamics manages the general administrative, financial and logistical support requirements of our wholly owned subsidiaries.
The SCS subsidiary is developing a hydrocarbon concession that is located offshore the Republic of Guinea in West Africa. The concession is one of the largest exploration areas in the world. Our current development program is engaged in the acquisition, processing, and interpretation of seismic data. SCS Corp. expects to commence a drilling program upon completion of its seismic evaluation.
HYD Resources is primarily engaged in the operation of domestic drilling and exploration in the southern United States. The company currently owns two drilling rigs, which are employed for contract fees, joint ventures and in-house projects.
Trendsetter Production company is an oil and gas leasing company that currently holds leases across the southern united states.

Cityview is a vertically integrated real estate investment manager based in Los Angeles with offices in Dallas and New York. The firm specializes in developing and acquiring multifamily projects across the risk spectrum. Since its founding in 2003, Cityview has invested approximately $7 billion in more than 150 projects across the United States and has operated and developed nearly 20,000 units. The firm manages approximately 7,500 multifamily units, with over 1,700 units in active renovations and more than 2,600 units under development. The company operates with a data-driven investment strategy across Western and Southwestern U.S. markets. Cityview recently expanded to the East Coast with a New York City office, targeting markets including Boston, Atlanta, and Orlando. The firm closed its seventh discretionary fund in 2024 and completed several projects, including a 265-unit multifamily community in Los Angeles' South Bay. Westhome Property Management serves as Cityview's affiliated property management company. The firm maintains a focus on locations with strong job and population growth and diverse economies.

Trico Marine Group offers an array of specialized services and superior vessels and equipment, along with a global team of experienced, innovative, project-driven professionals. Our depth of experience and expertise in both vessel and subsea service operations allows us to offer our customers packaged solutions or individual vessel and service offerings in markets worldwide. We are ready to support your next offshore or subsea project efficiently and seamlessly, anytime and anyplace.

Epiq began in 1988 in Kansas City as a bankruptcy services company and later combined with DTI under the Epiq name. The company now operates as a global provider of legal and compliance services, integrating people, process, and technology to support large-scale legal and business workflows. Its services cover eDiscovery, litigation support, class action and mass tort administration, court reporting, regulatory compliance, restructuring, bankruptcy, legal transformation, and other business operations. Epiq also continues to invest in services-enabled technology, including proprietary AI and SaaS offerings, as part of its current legal solutions focus.

Havas Paris is a French creative communications agency within the Havas global communications group, and its work spans creative strategy, brand consulting, digital and content, events, reputation and influence, international communications, and public affairs. The agency operates as a strategic creative shop with a multidisciplinary model that brings together brand, media, PR, content, and engagement work for clients. Havas traces its roots to the Paris-founded Havas news and communications business created in 1835, which later evolved into the modern Havas group. Today, Havas Paris sits inside a wider communications network with a broad international presence and a range of services for brands and institutions.

At RSI, we understand your need to help clients close deals without any unnecessary setbacks. Our team has over 100 years of combined experience in national public record research, court information systems and title analysis. This type of research is an art and a science. It takes tenacious, experienced professionals, and our team does it better than anyone else. 
Using our exclusive, state-of-the-art RapidDoc™ system, we are able to complete detailed Property Research Reports quickly without compromising quality. There's a reason we call it RapidDoc™. Our reports are typically completed within 24 hours in most metropolitan areas. Many are even completed within the same day we receive a request. RSI is beating the odds and redefining risk management.

Target Corporation began in 1902 as the Dayton Company and later launched Target stores in the 1960s; Dayton Hudson Corporation adopted the Target Corporation name in 2000. The company operates a broad retail business centered on discount general merchandise, everyday essentials, apparel, beauty, home goods, food and beverages, plus digital shopping, fulfillment, and loyalty services. Target serves guests through stores and digital channels across the United States, with a business model built around curated assortment, value, and integrated shopping experiences.

Emanuel Real Estate Group is a real estate company with 1 employee(s). Hooman Emanuel is the Broker. This company has been part of Connected Investors since 05/15/2017 - Emanuel Real Estate Group Based out of . Connect with the employees and team members of Emanuel Real Estate Group on Connected Investors.

Walgreens began in 1901 when pharmacist Charles R. Walgreen Sr. opened a neighborhood drugstore on Chicago's South Side, and the business later formed Walgreens Boots Alliance through a full combination with Alliance Boots in 2014. The company operates a broad retail pharmacy network and offers prescriptions, health services, clinical care initiatives, and everyday retail products alongside pharmaceutical wholesaling and related supply chain activity. The company has expanded its role in pharmacy and retail health to include delivery, vaccination, digital care tools, and other services connected to community pharmacy care.

Curves began in 1992 as a women’s fitness concept created to offer a safe, supportive space for exercise, and the brand later expanded into an international franchise network. The company’s core business centers on women-focused fitness clubs that combine a 30-minute circuit workout with strength training, cardio, stretching, and coach support at each session. Curves also offers franchise opportunities and an online fitness platform, extending the business beyond in-club memberships into digital workout access. Public company materials describe Curves as a long-running women’s fitness brand built around community-oriented wellness programs.

The company’s core business centers on women-focused fitness clubs that combine a 30-minute circuit workout with strength training, cardio, stretching, and coach support at each session. Curves also offers franchise opportunities and an online fitness platform, extending the business beyond in-club memberships into digital workout access. Mail Boxes Etc., Inc., a UPS company, is the world's largest franchisor of retail shipping, postal and business service centers. The UPS Store and Mail Boxes Etc. retail centers together comprise more than 5,300 independently owned locations around the world, providing convenient, value-added business services to consumers, road warriors and the small-office/home-office (SOHO) market.

Zales began in 1924 when Morris M. Zale, William Zale, and Ben Lipshy opened the first Zales Jewelers store in Wichita Falls, Texas. The company grew through an early credit plan that helped make jewelry more accessible, and it later expanded beyond its original Texas base into a broader North American retail presence. Today, Zales focuses on fine jewelry across categories such as engagement rings, wedding bands, natural and lab-grown diamonds, necklaces, earrings, bracelets, watches, and personalized pieces. The company offers online shopping and store-based services, keeping its business centered on jewelry retail for everyday wear and major life events.

KAY Jewelers began in Reading, Pennsylvania in 1916 and has grown into a jewelry retailer focused on fine jewelry, watches, and related services. The company offers engagement rings, wedding bands, natural and lab-grown diamonds, necklaces, earrings, bracelets, gemstone jewelry, personalized gifts, and watches, along with jewelry repair, watch repair, ring sizing, engraving, custom design, cleaning, and inspection services. KAY is part of Signet Jewelers and maintains a broad retail presence across the United States through its store network and online shopping. The company operates an Ohio location serving the Fairlawn area.

Hooters began in 1983 with the opening of the first restaurant in Clearwater, Florida, and the brand later grew into a franchised casual dining business. Hooters of America serves as the franchisor and operator of Hooters and Hoots Wings by Hooters, with a menu centered on chicken wings, burgers, sandwiches, drinks, and catering. The company also emphasizes sports viewing, takeout, delivery, gift cards, and loyalty programs through its digital channels. Public company materials describe a wide restaurant network in the United States and abroad, while Wikipedia notes the brand’s long-running presence as an international restaurant chain.

Chipotle Mexican Grill began in 1993 with a single restaurant and grew into a fast-casual restaurant company centered on burritos, burrito bowls, tacos, quesadillas, and salads. Chipotle emphasizes responsibly sourced ingredients, classic cooking methods, and a customizable ordering style built around made-to-order meals. The company operates a broad restaurant network in the United States and also serves international markets through company-owned and partner-operated restaurants. Chipotle supports digital ordering, delivery, catering, rewards, fundraising, and sustainability programs as part of its broader business model.

Morton's The Steakhouse began as a Chicago steakhouse in 1978 and now operates a wide network of restaurants in the United States and beyond. The company focuses on USDA prime-aged steak, fresh seafood, poultry, and a broad wine program, alongside cocktails and desserts. Morton's also offers private dining and event service for business meetings, celebrations, and other group occasions. The brand has remained centered on classic steakhouse dining while expanding into lunch, happy hour, catering, and event-focused formats.

ACT and its affiliates own, operate, and/or license other convenience store brands including Circle K, Couche-Tard, Macs, Kangaroo Express, and Corner Store.  

ACT acquired the On the Run sites and brand name in the U.S. in 2009.  Today, the majority have been converted to Circle K company-operated sites, but a number of On the Run franchise locations remain open in various parts of the U.S.

CheckFree (NASDAQ: CKFR) is a provider of financial electronic commerce services and products. From powering electronic billing and payment, to automating financial transactions, to streamlining regulatory reporting tasks, CheckFree's broad range of solutions continue to set new standards for quality. 
At CheckFree, our vision is to make complex financial activities easier for businesses and consumers. For 25 years, we've been turning that vision into a reality by setting the standard for leadership, innovation and quality of financial electronic commerce. Today, CheckFree provides software and services to thousands of businesses and millions of consumers everyday.

Lumen Technologies, formerly CenturyLink, began in 1930 as a Louisiana telephone company and later expanded through a series of mergers and business changes. Lumen Technologies now operates as an enterprise technology and telecommunications company focused on connecting people, data, and applications. The company provides networking, edge cloud, collaboration, cybersecurity, managed services, and related digital infrastructure for business customers. Lumen Technologies also positions its portfolio around secure networking and AI-ready infrastructure, with a market presence built on fiber-based connectivity and enterprise services.

TeamGerber comprises passionate, seasoned professionals who have worked for the “big firms.” We have several staff members with advanced degrees and certifications. Additionally, our Premier International membership brings you access to outstanding professionals globally and nationally — yet we provide the culture and the pricing structure of a local firm.

La-Z-Boy began in 1927 in Monroe, Michigan, when Edward Knabusch and Edwin Shoemaker developed the reclining chair that became the company’s signature product. Today, the company operates as a vertically integrated retailer and manufacturer, handling retail, manufacturing, design, distribution, and after-service care for home furnishings. La-Z-Boy’s portfolio includes the La-Z-Boy brand along with Joybird, England Furniture, Hammary, Kincaid, and American Drew, covering upholstered furniture, casegoods, and custom pieces for multiple rooms in the home. The business continues to focus on recliners, sofas, chairs, ottomans, and other home-furnishing categories through retail, wholesale, and digital channels.

profile.locationBio: Staffmark began as a staffing business with more than 55 years of history and now operates under the Staffmark brand after combining former Advantage Resourcing and Pro Staff business lines. The company connects employers with talent through temporary staffing, direct hire, and customized workforce solutions. Its services also include onsite solutions, managed services, outsourcing, and performance management for clients with changing labor needs. Staffmark serves employers and job seekers through a broad staffing platform built around recruiting, placement, and workforce support.

profile.locationBio: Kevin Jewelers is a jewelry retailer founded in 1975 in California. The company began as a small 300-square-foot store and has grown into one of Southern California’s largest family-owned jewelry chains. Specializing in engagement rings, wedding bands, certified diamonds, and luxury watches, Kevin Jewelers operates 40 retail locations across California. The company also offers in-house financing and services such as jewelry repair, trade-ins, and diamond upgrades. Known for its commitment to affordability and quality, Kevin Jewelers has maintained its original philosophy of “Your best price, our family’s promise” for nearly five decades.

Gateway Energy LLC is a natural gas infrastructure company that owns and operates gathering, transmission, and distribution systems. The company focuses on moving natural gas to industrial end users and maintains assets across Texas, Arkansas, Missouri, and New York. Gateway Energy LLC was organized as a Delaware company and registered in Texas as a foreign limited liability company, reflecting an origin in midstream energy operations rather than retail energy sales. Its asset portfolio includes systems serving industrial and processing facilities, which places the company in the natural gas transportation and delivery segment of the energy market.

NTT DATA Group Corporation began operations in 1988 as a spin-off from NTT and has since grown into a global IT and business services firm. The company provides consulting, industry solutions, business process services, IT modernization, managed services, and connectivity support for clients across a wide range of industries. NTT DATA Group operates within the NTT Group and serves a broad international customer base through its business and technology offerings. The company maintains an established year of 1988 and focuses on helping organizations transform through digital services and technology-driven operations.

Chase, the consumer and commercial banking brand of JPMorganChase, offers checking and savings accounts, credit cards, home loans, auto financing, and business banking services. Chase traces its roots to New York City's first water company in 1799, and the modern bank grew through the history of heritage firms including The Manhattan Company and Chase Manhattan Bank, the former name used before the merger with J.P. Morgan & Co. Chase now serves millions of people with a broad range of financial products and a significant branch and ATM network in the United States, while JPMorganChase operates across consumer, business, and institutional banking lines.

The Houston Independent School District is the largest public school system in Texas and the seventh-largest in the United States. Its schools are dedicated to giving every student the best possible education through an intensive core curriculum and specialized, challenging instructional and career programs. HISD is working hard to become Houstonians' K–12 school system of choice, by constantly improving instruction and management to be as effective, productive, and economical as possible.
HISD set specific goals and a detailed blueprint was designed to reach them. In 1990, the HISD Board of Education drafted A Declaration of Beliefs and Visions. This call for districtwide change has been the driving force behind many of the district's improvements, and in 2001 and in 2004, the board reaffirmed its commitment to the goals and strategies outlined in that landmark document.

Publicis Groupe is a French communications company that began in 1926 and has grown into a multinational business focused on advertising, public relations, media, and marketing services. The company operates on a connected platform that brings together capabilities across Publicis Communications, Publicis Media, Publicis Sapient, and Publicis Health, with services that combine creativity, technology, and data. In Australia and New Zealand, Publicis Groupe ANZ functions as a connected platform of companies and capabilities, supported by a portfolio of agency brands and work across creative, media, and digital business transformation.

AIR Communities, formerly Apartment Income REIT Corp., is a multifamily real estate company that owns and operates rental housing communities across the United States. The company was formed in 2020 and operated as a publicly traded REIT (NYSE: AIRC) until June 2024, when Blackstone Real Estate Partners X completed its privatization of the company in an all-cash transaction valued at $10 billion, including debt. Headquartered in Denver, Colorado, AIR Communities focuses on coastal markets apartment homes located in 10 states and the District of Columbia. Primary markets include Miami, Los Angeles, Boston, and Washington D.C. The company operates under a business model centered on resident selection, satisfaction, and retention, coupled with property management practices designed to drive organic growth. Following the Blackstone acquisition, the private equity firm committed to investing more than $400 million to maintain and improve the existing portfolio. AIR Communities is now owned by Blackstone and operates as a private entity with a focus on multifamily rental housing in markets where apartment demand generates continued growth.

Citi began in 1812 and has grown from early banking roots into a global financial services firm with a broad international presence. The company provides consumer banking, cards, wealth and lending services, along with institutional offerings such as markets, banking, services, and treasury and trade solutions. Citi also supports clients with payments, liquidity management, investor services, and issuer services through its business lines. Its modern form emerged from the 1998 merger of Citicorp and Travelers, while the Citi brand reflects a long history of expanding financial services across markets and customer segments.

Bolt Technology Corporation consists of four operating units: Bolt Technology Corporation (“Bolt”), A-G Geophysical Products, Inc. (“A-G”), Real Time Systems Inc. (“RTS”) and SeaBotix Inc. (“SBX”). Each of these operating units is reported as a separate reportable segment for all periods presented in the Consolidated Financial Statements. Bolt, A-G and RTS products are used in marine seismic exploration surveys to acquire seismic data. Bolt develops, manufactures and sells marine seismic energy sources (air guns) and replacement parts and is referred to as the “seismic energy sources” segment.

Portsmouth Square, Inc. is a California corporation, incorporated in 1967. Portsmouth is a public company that trades on the OTCBB under the symbol "PRSI", and is a consolidated subsidiary of The InterGroup Corporation and Santa Fe Financial Corporation.

Allstate began in 1931 as an insurance business created within Sears, Roebuck and Co., and later became an independent publicly traded company. The company is primarily engaged in property and casualty insurance in the United States and Canada, and also offers life, accident and health insurance, along with protection plans for electronic devices and personal identities. Allstate's product set includes auto, home, rental, motorcycle, business insurance, roadside services, embedded insurance, and related protection solutions delivered through a broad distribution network. Over time, the business has expanded beyond its original auto-insurance roots into a wider protection platform centered on personal and commercial coverage.

Internet America, Inc. is an internet service provider ("ISP") focused on providing wireless high-speed broadband internet in rural markets. As of June 30, 2014, we served approximately 25,700 total subscribers in Texas, Oklahoma and Missouri. Our corporate headquarters are located in Houston, Texas, where our executive functions, call center and network monitoring systems reside. We are a corporation organized under the laws of the state of Texas that was formed in 1995.We offer broadband internet services to customers within our network footprint, primarily focusing on rural, residential markets. We install wireless internet service in communities and rural areas that have little or no access to alternative broadband solutions.

The attorneys at Summers Levine Lipsic & Hersh LLP successfully represent their clients in cases involving complex and high conflict family law cases, including child custody and visitation issues, division of high-net-worth estates, domestic violence, dependency matters, guardianships, mediations, and prenuptial and postnuptial agreements. The firm's founding partners and attorneys share a passion for bringing the highest level of professionalism and ethical standards to every family law matter.

Sanes, Matthews & Forester's philosophy is to never forget we exist to serve the needs of our clients. We help those unable to help themselves in what is often the most stressful period of their lives. For over a decade the attorneys in our office have fought for the individual's rights all over Texas. From Lubbock to Brownsville, from Lufkin to El Paso, we have represented injured victims against negligent corporations, doctors, truck drivers, insurance companies and manufacturers of dangerous products. We represent individuals who have been injured in accidents ranging from automobile / tractor-trailor collisions to aviation catastrophies.
Though we specialize in handling cases involving catastrophic injuries and death, we also represent clients with less severe injuries in the same conscientious manner. Our firm is equipped to handle a broad range of injury cases in areas of complex products liability, on-the-job injuries, medical negligence, oil rig accidents and more.

PBK began in 1981 as an architectural planning and design firm with a focus on educational facilities. The firm now provides integrated architecture, engineering, interior design, planning, technology, and facilities consulting services across education, sports, civic, healthcare, and corporate project types. PBK operates through a national network of offices and positions its work around coordinated design, planning, and client service for communities across the country.

For the past 20 years, MacFarlane Partners has provided investment management services for institutional clients across a broad range of real estate investment strategies, helping them achieve returns that have exceeded all relevant performance benchmarks.
Founded in 1987, the firm has successfully developed, acquired, renovated, managed and sold real estate assets through multiple real estate cycles on behalf of some of the largest pension plans in the United States.
It currently focuses on two high-yielding investment strategies that are derived from its core competencies in property development, smart growth/urban revitalization and single-family homebuilding.

Each patient and his or her story is uniquely different. Why shouldn't treatments then be equally individualized?

Dr. St. John begins consultations with an hour long comprehensive evaluation and creates an individualized treatment plan for each patient considering the patient's unique biology, psychological strengths and challenges, social environment, and treatment goals. Psychotropic genetic testing is routinely ordered via saliva sample collection in the office. Genetic testing can help guide Dr. St. John in determining which medications and at which doses may work best, taking some of the trial and error out of the medication selection process.

Subway began in 1965 as Pete's Super Submarine Sandwiches, founded by Fred DeLuca with support from Peter Buck, and later adopted the Subway name. The company has grown into a large restaurant franchise built around made-to-order sandwiches, wraps, salads, and other quick-service menu items. Subway restaurants are owned and operated by a broad franchise network, and the brand emphasizes fresh bread, customizable meals, and convenient service for everyday dining. The company continues to serve guests across a wide international restaurant system while remaining focused on its core sandwich-shop format.

Regions Bank began in 1971 as First Alabama Bankshares after a merger involving three Alabama banks, and the business later adopted the Regions name as it expanded beyond its original base. The company operates as a full-service financial institution offering consumer and commercial banking, wealth management, and mortgage products and services, with personal banking, digital banking, and branch-based support among its core customer offerings. Regions maintains a broader community-focused presence through engagement and inclusion initiatives that support customers, associates, and local communities. Its market footprint extends across the South, Midwest, and Texas, giving the firm a wide regional reach in everyday banking and broader financial services.

The company has grown into a large restaurant franchise built around made-to-order sandwiches, wraps, salads, and other quick-service menu items. Subway restaurants are owned and operated by a broad franchise network, and the brand emphasizes fresh bread, customizable meals, and convenient service for everyday dining. Walker Consultants began in 1965 as a structural engineering firm and later expanded into parking design and consulting. The company now offers services across parking design, planning and mobility, operations and technology, building envelope, building systems, due diligence, forensics, restoration, and vertical transportation. Walker Consultants brings together planners, designers, engineers, architects, and technical specialists to support projects involving uncertainty, existing conditions, and long-term asset performance. The company remains employee-owned and is recognized among the notable names in parking structure design and consulting.

Lederer & Nojima is a California-based law firm specializing in personal injury cases. The firm's attorneys leverage their experience as former insurance defense lawyers to advocate for injury victims. Practice areas include automobile accidents, wrongful death claims, and premises liability disputes. The firm operates on contingency fees, ensuring clients only pay upon winning their cases. Lederer & Nojima emphasizes personalized service and has a track record of recovering compensation for clients across Southern California.

Wells Fargo began in 1852 as a bank and express company serving the needs of the California Gold Rush and later evolved into a full-service financial institution. The company now offers consumer banking, commercial banking, corporate and investment banking, and wealth and investment management, with products that include deposit accounts, lending, mortgages, credit cards, treasury management, and investing services. Wells Fargo maintains a broad national and global business presence built through years of expansion and mergers, while continuing to emphasize financial services for households, businesses, and communities.

JPMorgan Chase began in 1799 through the founding of the Bank of the Manhattan Company, and the modern firm took shape in 2000 through the merger of Chase Manhattan and J.P. Morgan. The company operates as a financial holding company with businesses in consumer and community banking, commercial and investment banking, asset and wealth management, and financial transaction processing. JPMorgan Chase serves millions of consumers, small businesses, corporations, institutional clients, and government clients through a broad mix of banking, lending, investing, payments, and treasury services. The firm maintains a broad market presence in the United States and abroad, with operations across many global markets and a long-running focus on financial services for households, businesses, and institutions.

Fifth Third Bank traces its roots to the Bank of the Ohio Valley and later became Fifth Third National before adopting the Fifth Third Bank name. The company provides consumer and business banking, commercial banking, wealth management, mortgage lending, and payments-related services, with offerings spanning everyday banking, financing, and advisory needs. Fifth Third Bank has served customers since 1858 and now serves individuals, businesses, and communities through a broad U.S. banking network and digital channels.

Northwestern Mutual, formerly The Northwestern Mutual Life Insurance Company, began in Wisconsin in 1857 and grew from its mutual insurance roots into a financial services company. The company offers life insurance, disability insurance, long-term care protection, annuities, and investment-related services through a range of planning and advisory offerings. Northwestern Mutual also serves clients through wealth, estate, retirement, and business planning services, while maintaining a mutual structure that places policyowners at the center of its business model.

BNY, formerly BNY Mellon, traces its roots to the Bank of New York, founded in 1784, and later combined with Mellon Financial Corporation in 2007 to form the company in its current structure. The company operates as a global financial services platforms business, providing custody, clearing, collateral management, issuer services, asset servicing, and related solutions across the financial lifecycle. BNY serves clients around the world through technology and market infrastructure capabilities designed to help move, manage, and safeguard assets, with its current brand reflecting an updated naming approach that shortened the legacy BNY Mellon identity to BNY.

Spherion is a staffing and workforce solutions company that has been serving businesses and job seekers since its founding in 1946. Originally established as City Car Unloaders in Chicago, the company evolved through several name changes and acquisitions before adopting the Spherion brand in 2000. Headquartered in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, Spherion operates as part of Randstad NV, a global leader in human resource services. The company provides a range of services, including temporary staffing, direct-hire placements, executive search, and recruitment process outsourcing, catering to diverse industries across the United States. Spherion’s business model combines corporate support with a network of local franchise owners, enabling it to deliver personalized staffing solutions. Over the decades, the company has expanded its footprint nationwide and continues to focus on matching skilled talent with employers.

Duane Morris began in Philadelphia in 1904 as Duane, Morris, Heckscher & Roberts, and the firm’s history reflects a long expansion from a local partnership into a broad legal practice. Duane Morris is a law firm with more than 900 attorneys serving clients across the United States and internationally, and the firm says its modern organization reaches across the U.S., Europe, and Asia. The firm’s work spans litigation, corporate matters, immigration, products liability, and other business and regulatory services for a wide range of clients. Duane Morris also maintains a global footprint through offices and lawyers qualified in multiple jurisdictions, supporting cross-border matters for commercial and institutional clients.

JPMorgan Chase serves millions of consumers, small businesses, corporations, institutional clients, and government clients through a broad mix of banking, lending, investing, payments, and treasury services. The firm maintains a broad market presence in the United States and abroad, with operations across many global markets and a long-running focus on financial services for households, businesses, and institutions.

C.H. Guenther began in 1851 when the Guenther family opened for business and Carl Hilmar Guenther built a flour mill near Fredericksburg, Texas, before moving production to San Antonio as the business grew. The company later expanded from milling into consumer convenience foods and foodservice, building a broader portfolio over time. Today, C.H. Guenther serves retail and foodservice channels with products that include appetizers, bakery items, baking and griddle mixes, biscuits, buns and English muffins, desserts, flour, tortillas, pizza dough, gravies, sauces, seasonings, and dips. The company continues to position itself around food solutions, culinary innovation, and product development for a wide range of meal occasions.

Fidelity National Title Insurance Company traces origins back to mid-19th-century title businesses and later began doing business in Nebraska in the early 1960s. The company became part of Fidelity National Financial in the 1980s and now operates through underwriting subsidiaries within a nationwide network of direct operations and agents. Fidelity National Title Insurance Company provides title insurance, underwriting, escrow, and closing services for residential, commercial, and industrial clients, along with related services such as recordings, reconveyances, flood certification, trust activities, and real estate tax service. The business also serves lenders, developers, attorneys, real estate professionals, and consumers, and offers commercial real estate services through national commercial teams.

profile.locationBio: Ricoh began in 1936 as a spin-off from the sensitized paper division of Rikagaku Kogyo and grew from early imaging roots into a global business technology company. The company's business domains include digital services, digital products, graphic communications, and industrial solutions, covering multifunction printers, printers, scanners, network equipment, software, and industrial printing systems. Ricoh also serves workplaces with applications, support, and service solutions, and its operations reach customers across a broad international network.

Hill & Knowlton began in Cleveland in 1927 and has grown into a global strategic communications consultancy. The company works across corporate communications, reputation and crisis issues, digital and creative campaign development, and data-informed strategy. Its sector focus includes financial and professional services, health and wellness, and other industry-specific communications needs. Hill & Knowlton is a firm built around transformation, helping organizations shape stakeholder relationships and support business goals across a broad international network.

Kelly Services began in 1946 when William Russell Kelly launched the business in Detroit as an office service that connected workers with employers. The company has since grown into a workforce solutions firm serving professional, industrial, IT, engineering, and specialized talent needs through temporary staffing, direct hire, recruitment process outsourcing, managed service programs, and statement-of-work management. The company has sharpened its focus on specialty outcome-based and staffing services in North America, while maintaining global recruitment process outsourcing and managed service capabilities.

Energy Intelligence Group, Inc. was formed in 1996 through the combination of Oil Daily and Petroleum Intelligence Weekly, building on publications that began in the early 1950s and 1960s. The company provides news, analysis, research, data, and advisory services across oil markets, gas and LNG, low-carbon energy, risk, and competitive intelligence. Energy Intelligence focuses on objective reporting and tailored intelligence for energy decision-makers, with offerings that include premium content, research, and industry events. The business serves a broad international energy audience and maintains a wide market presence through its editorial and advisory platform.

Fastrac began in 1998 through a merger of Bull Bros. Inc., Clark's Petroleum, and Glider Oil Co., and the brand later became part of EG America after EG Group acquired the business in 2019. The company operates as a convenience and retail brand with offerings that include fuel, coffee, made-to-order foodservice, pizza, and traditional convenience-store merchandise. Fastrac also supports digital ordering, a loyalty app, and business fuel card services, while maintaining a significant presence across upstate New York.

Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC) is the State of Texas agency responsible for administering health and human services programs that support millions of Texans. HHSC oversees Medicaid, behavioral health, disability services, long-term care, public assistance programs, and community support initiatives. Through a statewide network of offices, facilities, providers, and partnerships, the agency works to improve health outcomes, strengthen communities, and help Texans access essential services and resources.

At Union Pacific Railroad, they're prepared to ship just about anything: food, forest products, automobiles, agricultural products, coal and chemicals – safely and on time. No rail? No problem. Their shipping capabilities are not limited to their extensive system map. they will coordinate your shipment through our network, through other railroads and over the road, providing complete, door-to-door service. They offer their customers the most efficient, environmentally friendly transportation solutions available today.

profile.locationBio: Konica Minolta traces its origins to 1873, when Konica began selling photographic and lithographic materials in Tokyo, while Minolta's precursor emerged in the late 1920s and the two businesses merged in 2003. The company now focuses on office technology, managed print services, IT services, enterprise content management, industrial and commercial printing, and packaging solutions. Konica Minolta also operates healthcare and sensing businesses, with offerings that include medical imaging solutions and optical color-and-light measurement products. In the United States, the company supports digital transformation through business solutions, office automation, and a broad portfolio of products and services for commercial and industrial customers.

PNC Financial Services Group traces roots to nineteenth-century Pennsylvania banks and took its current shape through a 1983 merger between Pittsburgh National Corporation and Provident National Corporation. PNC is one of the largest diversified financial services institutions in the United States and provides retail and business banking, lending, corporate banking, real estate finance, asset-based lending, wealth management, and asset management. The company serves individuals, small businesses, corporations, and government entities through a broad mix of banking and financial services that supports consumer, commercial, and institutional needs.

Skyline Deli & Cafe began serving customers in 1994 and describes itself as Houston’s original office building deli. Skyline Deli & Cafe focuses on fast-casual food service with made-to-order sandwiches, wraps, salads, burgers, and breakfast items such as tacos and croissants. The company also provides catering and online ordering, and the menu includes coffee, lunch options, and digital gift cards. Skyline Deli & Cafe presents its business as a neighborhood deli and cafe built around quick service and a broad mix of breakfast and lunch offerings.

Integrity was formed in 2003 by Richard Aguilar, Melanie Bailey and K.C. Griffin with the idea that apartments could be managed better. 
After over a decade of working with different management companies, multiple owners and diverse properties, Melanie and K.C. had a vision of working with an owner whose desire was to keep apartments,improve the quality of apartment living and take a long term approach to management. They wanted a permanent plan with someone invested in El Paso.
Richard Aguilar is a native El Pasoan who began his real estate career as a teenager. He had a desire to change the face of El Paso by buying, improving and building apartment housing for the long haul. Having contracted with several different management companies before, Richard knew that having the right people in place was key to achieving his goals. After working with Melanie and K.C. for several years, the decision to move forward with Integrity was made and the growth has been unprecedented since.

You can even reach in-market renters with search ads, social ads and email marketing solutions that are powered by their marketplace.

Shell formed in 1907 through the merger of Royal Dutch Petroleum and the Shell Transport and Trading Company, creating a business that grew into a global energy group. Shell's operations span exploration, production, refining, marketing, chemicals, and trading, alongside lower-carbon areas such as biofuels, solar, wind, and electric vehicle charging. In the United States, Shell has been active for more than a century with every major line of business represented in the country, including oil and gas production, retail fuels, LNG, pipelines, and renewables. Shell also maintains a broad market presence through Shell-branded fuel stations and energy supply activities across the country.

Shintech is a chemical manufacturer focused on polyvinyl chloride resin and chlor-alkali products, with production tied to PVC, vinyl chloride monomer, and caustic soda. The company's history traces back to the 1970s in Texas, when PVC production began under a joint venture and later moved under Shin-Etsu Chemical ownership. Shintech operates facilities in Texas and Louisiana and centers its business around safe, environmentally responsible operations, community support, and supply to daily-use and industrial materials markets.

Bankers Life began as the predecessor to Bankers Life and Casualty Company in 1879 and later became a marketing brand within CNO Financial Group. The company focuses on insurance and retirement solutions for middle-income adults near or in retirement, with products that include Medicare Supplement insurance, long-term care insurance, life insurance, annuities, and related financial services. Bankers Life also includes affiliated securities, advisory, and wealth management services within the CNO family of brands, extending the business beyond core insurance offerings. Bankers Life operates as part of a broader insurance and financial services group serving customers across the United States.

Frito-Lay began in the early 1930s as two snack businesses founded by Charles Elmer Doolin and Herman W. Lay, and the companies merged in 1961 to form Frito-Lay, Inc. Frito-Lay became part of PepsiCo in 1965 and now operates as a snack foods business unit within PepsiCo's convenient foods portfolio. Frito-Lay makes and markets a wide range of savory snacks, including Lay's, Fritos, Doritos, Cheetos, Tostitos, SunChips, Ruffles, Rold Gold, Funyuns, and branded dips, with products sold through a broad distribution network in North America and beyond.

Kelly Services began in 1946 when William Russell Kelly launched the business in Detroit as an office service that connected workers with employers. The company has since grown into a workforce solutions firm serving professional, industrial, IT, engineering, and specialized talent needs through temporary staffing, direct hire, recruitment process outsourcing, managed service programs, and statement-of-work management. The company has sharpened its focus on specialty outcome-based and staffing services in North America, while maintaining global recruitment process outsourcing and managed service capabilities.

Energy Alloys Global Solutions traces its modern form to the BioUrja Group's expansion in corrosion-resistant metal alloy products and tubular goods, including the acquisition of Hamilton Metals and the international assets of Energy Alloys. The company focuses on in-house manufacturing and distribution solutions for tube and bar products, serving global oil and gas manufacturers and service companies. Its product and service mix includes carbon, alloy, stainless, nickel, and OCTG materials, along with inventory planning, machining, and turnkey component solutions. Energy Alloys Global Solutions maintains a global operating footprint with facilities in the United States, Mexico, the United Kingdom, Dubai, and Singapore.

Veris Residential was founded in 1997 and later operated as Mack-Cali Realty Corporation before adopting the Veris Residential name in 2021. Veris Residential develops, owns, acquires, and manages premier multifamily communities, with a portfolio centered on apartment homes and related retail assets in the Northeast. The company emphasizes sustainability-conscious design, community programs, and technology-enabled operations across a vertically integrated platform. In 2026, an investor consortium led by Affinius Capital and Vista Hill Partners completed an all-cash acquisition of the business, and the company's common stock ceased trading after the transaction closed.

profile.locationBio: Verizon began in 2000 through the merger of Bell Atlantic and GTE, forming a communications company that has since expanded beyond traditional telecom services. The company provides wireless connectivity, broadband, and fiber-based services for consumers and businesses, along with network and security solutions for enterprise customers. Verizon serves public-sector and large business customers through its Verizon Business unit, reflecting a broad mix of consumer, business, and network offerings. The company is a global communications technology company with a large market presence across mobility and broadband.

Ingersoll Rand traces its roots to nineteenth-century drill and compressor businesses that later merged into a broader industrial products company. The current business was formed through the combination of the industrial segment of the earlier Ingersoll-Rand business with Gardner Denver, bringing together a long operating history and a wide portfolio of brands. The company provides air, fluid, energy, and medical technologies, along with industrial, energy, medical, and specialty vehicle products and services. Ingersoll Rand serves customers across major global markets through more than forty brands and focuses on productivity, efficiency, and mission-critical applications where downtime is costly.

ONEOK began in 1906 as an intrastate natural gas pipeline business in Oklahoma and later adopted the ONEOK name from its former identity as Oklahoma Natural Gas Company. The company now operates as a midstream energy business with gathering, processing, fractionation, transportation, storage, and marine export services. Its asset base links supply basins with major market centers and supports the movement of natural gas, natural gas liquids, refined products, and crude oil across the United States. The firm maintains a broad market presence in the United States and abroad, with operations across many global markets and a long-running focus on financial services for households, businesses, and institutions.

Unlike other renal replacement devices currently on the market, the Xcorporeal devices are user friendly, lightweight, portable and eventually wearable, providing patients with continuous treatments (as opposed to intermittent) and allowing them to achieve a quality of life closer to that of a healthy individual.

Pediatric Home Service partners with families and healthcare professionals to enable children to live safely at home rather than in institutional settings. The organization is accredited by the Accreditation Commission for Health Care (ACHC) and operates multiple locations across the United States. Chevron began as Pacific Coast Oil Co. and later operated as Standard Oil of California before adopting the Chevron name. The company directly employs over twelve hundred fifty people and supports an additional fifteen hundred indirect employees. The firm describes itself as among the first to pursue complex Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) deals. Its LIHTC program began in 2011 and its workforce housing initiative in 2018. Within the real estate sector, the company maintains investment holdings in multifamily and affordable housing properties, with specialized focus on Low-Income Housing Tax Credit structures and workforce housing programs that serve moderate-income and low-income households. The real estate holdings operate across fourteen states with concentration in California and Texas markets, where the firm has assembled a portfolio through strategic acquisitions of existing apartment communities. The real estate operations are complemented by affiliated service companies providing property management, construction management, title services, and insurance coverage, creating an integrated platform across the ownership lifecycle.

Camden Property Trust is a publicly traded multifamily real estate investment trust focused on the ownership, management, development, and redevelopment of apartment communities across high-growth U.S. markets. Co-founded by Richard Campo and Keith Oden in 1982, the company went public in 1993 and has since become an S&P 500 component and one of the largest multifamily REITs in the United States. The company operates with a vertically integrated model, handling construction, leasing, maintenance, and resident services in-house rather than outsourcing to third-party managers.

Camden's portfolio is concentrated in Sun Belt and select Mid-Atlantic markets with strong employment growth, population migration, and household formation trends. Key markets include Houston, Dallas, Atlanta, Phoenix, Tampa, Washington DC, and Charlotte. The company primarily owns Class A and upper-tier Class B apartment communities positioned in suburban and urban-suburban locations. In February 2026, Camden announced plans to exit California entirely, selling 11 properties totaling approximately 3,600 units valued at $1.5 billion, with proceeds to be redeployed into higher-return Sun Belt markets where regulatory environments are more favorable.

The company pursues growth through three parallel pipelines: development of new communities, selective acquisitions of stabilized assets, and capital recycling through dispositions of older properties. Camden maintains a disciplined approach to market timing, having navigated the elevated multifamily supply deliveries of 2024 while positioning for improved fundamentals as new construction slows. The company's management team has exhibited exceptional continuity, with co-founders Campo and Oden leading strategy for over 40 years.

The New York Film Academy was founded by veteran producer Jerry Sherlock in 1992, who produced such classics as "The Hunt for the Red October". Inspired by the idea that to learn how to make movies, one must actually make movies, Sherlock and his colleagues designed a truly unique curriculum. Blending a mixture of traditional film school instruction with a new approach, the Academy emphasizes coursework based around students actually going out and shooting films as part of their coursework. Students write, produce, direct, and edit their own original films while also serving as crewmembers on their fellow classmates' films to gain extensive on-set experience.

Its asset classes are multifamily and build-to-rent housing, grocery-anchored and power retail centers, industrial and office parks, and residential land. The company reports 13,024 apartments, 9,600,000 sf of retail built, 5,700,853 sf of office and industrial built, and 4,204 acres of planned communities in development. Its pipeline includes 633 rental homes, 2,200,000 sf of retail, 20,014 home sites and 320 acres of office and industrial land.

All holdings are in California and Nevada. Of the 37 apartment communities Lewis Apartments lists, 21 are in the Inland Empire (10 of them in Rancho Cucamonga), 8 are in Northern California and 7 are in Nevada. Goal: Understand What A Custom Suit Is And Whether It's For You.
Ordering a custom suit involves getting measured by a tailor, who then creates a pattern specific to your body. He or she uses that pattern to cut the fabric and then sews the suit by hand. Custom tailoring is often referred to as "bespoke," an old tailoring term meaning that a certain fabric has been "spoken for" by a customer and is therefore no longer for sale. 
What makes a bespoke suit different from one bought at a department store may be imperceptible at first glance: It's all in the fit and the details. Just about every man looks better in clothing that was made just for him, because custom tailoring takes into consideration the asymmetry of the wearer's body. Most men have one shoulder or hip that's higher than the other, or one arm or leg that's longer, for example. If your weight fluctuates wildly, however, custom-made may be a bad investment.

The company pursues growth through three parallel pipelines: development of new communities, selective acquisitions of stabilized assets, and capital recycling through dispositions of older properties. Lyvwell Apartments operates as the residential housing division and subsidiary of Brookfield Asset Management. The company manages over 20,000 multifamily units across North America, with a growing international presence. Lyvwell's multifamily business focuses on acquiring properties on a value basis and enhancing returns through active asset management.
The firm's investment approach centers on deploying capital during market dislocations. Between 2021 and 2022, Lyvwell sold $10 billion of U.S. multifamily assets at an average in-place cap rate of 3.7 percent. Starting in 2024, the company reversed course and deployed $3.7 billion to acquire or contract multifamily properties, capitalizing on distressed sales and valuation declines from 2022 peaks. Recent purchases have averaged cap rates nearly 200 basis points higher than prior dispositions. The portfolio includes both market-rate and rent-controlled properties, with concentrations in gateway cities and Sun Belt markets.
In November 2024, Lyvwell Apartments acquired eight properties totaling 4,143 units from Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust for $845 million, with assets located in Las Vegas, Phoenix, Columbus, Charlotte, and Chapel Hill. In early 2024, Lyvwell acquired a portfolio of approximately 2,100 multifamily apartments in San Francisco. The development pipeline includes 8,000+ units in planning and active construction stages, with an additional 15,000 units under development as of early 2026. United Cerebral Palsy (UCP) may be one of the largest health nonprofits in the U.S. today, but that was not the case in 1949. In the 1940s, there were not many options for families of and people with cerebral palsy and other disabilities.
Faced with fear and a lack of understanding by both the medical community and the general public, individuals with a disability were relegated to second-class status. Medical professionals frequently urged parents to warehouse their children in institutions where they lived out their lives, segregated from the rest of society. Parents who chose to raise their children at home learned that few services and supports were available to help their children lead full, productive lives in the community. With little contact between families of children with cerebral palsy, many parents felt isolated, helpless and alone.

Camden Property Trust is a publicly traded multifamily real estate investment trust focused on the ownership, management, development, and redevelopment of apartment communities across high-growth U.S. markets. The company operates with a vertically integrated model, handling construction, leasing, maintenance, and resident services in-house rather than outsourcing to third-party managers.

Camden's portfolio is concentrated in Sun Belt and select Mid-Atlantic markets with strong employment growth, population migration, and household formation trends. Key markets include Houston, Dallas, Atlanta, Phoenix, Tampa, Washington DC, and Charlotte. The company primarily owns Class A and upper-tier Class B apartment communities positioned in suburban and urban-suburban locations. In February 2026, Camden announced plans to exit California entirely, selling 11 properties totaling approximately 3,600 units valued at $1.5 billion, with proceeds to be redeployed into higher-return Sun Belt markets where regulatory environments are more favorable.

The company pursues growth through three parallel pipelines: development of new communities, selective acquisitions of stabilized assets, and capital recycling through dispositions of older properties. Camden maintains a disciplined approach to market timing, having navigated the elevated multifamily supply deliveries of 2024 while positioning for improved fundamentals as new construction slows. The company's management team has exhibited exceptional continuity, with co-founders Campo and Oden leading strategy for over 40 years.

Apartment Investment and Management Company, trading under the ticker AIV on the New York Stock Exchange, operates as a real estate investment trust with a portfolio centered on multifamily properties across targeted U.S. markets. On February 6, 2026, Aimco's stockholders approved a Plan of Sale and Liquidation, shifting the company's strategic focus toward the orderly disposition of all assets to maximize shareholder returns. The liquidation process includes selling stabilized properties, development projects, and land holdings throughout 2026.
Aimco maintains regional offices in Denver, Colorado (headquarters), Washington, D.C., and Miami, Florida. The company operates through a value-add and opportunistic investment approach, targeting properties where operational improvements and capital investment can drive rent growth and asset appreciation. As of December 31, 2024, the portfolio consisted of 24 apartment communities totaling 5,243 apartment units, plus one hotel property. The geographic footprint spans key metropolitan areas including Miami, New York City, the Washington, D.C. metro area, Chicago, Denver, Colorado Springs, Boulder, Nashville, Atlanta, and California markets including San Diego and the San Francisco Bay Area.
During 2025, Aimco sold $1.26 billion in real estate assets, including properties in suburban Boston and the Brickell Assemblage in Miami. In 2026, the company has continued asset sales, closing on properties in Nashville, Plantation (Florida), and Aurora (Colorado) for $177.5 million, with an additional portfolio of seven Chicago-area apartment communities under contract for $455 million. The company employs approximately 50 full-time staff focused on executing the liquidation strategy.

Europe forms a large share of the platform. Growth beyond these core regions includes entry into India in 2022, Saudi Arabia in 2024 and Mexico in 2026, its 20th country. A dedicated data center business, announced in 2024, now reports a pipeline of more than 5 GW of planned capacity, including an 88 MW campus near Barcelona.

The firm started in Minnesota and expanded into market-rate housing in the mid-1980s. In the 1990s it turned to developing, buying, and rehabilitating properties financed with low-income housing tax credits (LIHTC). In 1999 the founders, along with Armand Brachman and Paul Sween, formed Dominium Development and Acquisition to pursue that strategy nationally.

Dominium owns, develops, and manages more than 40,000 apartment homes in over 220 communities across 19 states, housing both families and seniors. Most of the portfolio is garden-style, townhome, and mid-rise senior communities with rents tied to Area Median Income. The company has also done historic redevelopments and added built-to-rent single-family communities to its portfolio.

Growth comes from two channels: new construction financed through LIHTC and tax-exempt bonds and buying existing tax-credit properties, then resyndicating and renovating them to extend their affordability. Development, construction and architecture, and property management are handled in-house by more than 1,200 employees.

Five Guys began as a small carry-out burger business in Arlington, Virginia, and grew from a family operation into a franchised restaurant brand. The company focuses on made-to-order hamburgers, hot dogs, hand-cut fries cooked in peanut oil, and handspun milkshakes with customizable mix-ins. Five Guys builds its business around simple menu choices, fresh ingredients, and a consistent burger-and-fries format that supports its broad fast-casual presence. The brand also offers catering and online ordering, reflecting a restaurant model built around dine-in, takeout, and digital service.

Equity Residential began in 1969 when Sam Zell created Equity Finance and Management Company. The firm became a public REIT in 1993 after acquiring properties from Starwood Capital Group. Today, Equity Residential owns apartment communities in coastal cities and high-demand markets nationwide. Their portfolio includes high-rise buildings and mid-rise complexes with modern amenities. The company focuses on acquiring and managing properties that attract long-term renters in urban centers. Equity Residential operates as a real estate investment trust, allowing investors to buy shares in their apartment portfolio.

With almost 2M square feet of retail and office space, their Commercial team provides the best property management services for their tenants. What sets Moss & Company apart is their hands-on management approach. This hands-on approach provides our commercial tenants with the best service and their clients with the best investment returns. It is unparalleled in the Property Management Industry. After all, It’s Personal.

Windsor Property Management, operating as Windsor Communities, is the in-house property management subsidiary of GID, a privately held real estate investment and management firm. Founded in 1960 with the renovation of three apartment buildings in Cambridge, Massachusetts, Windsor has grown into one of the largest multifamily property management companies in the United States. The firm focuses exclusively on multifamily residential properties, owning and managing over 155 apartment communities comprising more than 58,000 units across 23 markets. Windsor operates in 16 states and Washington D.C., with concentrations in California, the Pacific Northwest, Texas, Florida, the Southeast, and the Northeast corridor. The company maintains a vertically integrated approach, owning all properties under management rather than providing third-party services. Recent expansion has been driven by GID's active acquisition strategy, with 2024 purchases totaling over $750 million in multifamily assets. The firm ranked #37 among the largest apartment managers in the 2025 NMHC rankings and has been recognized as the #1 property management company for resident satisfaction for five consecutive years.

In 1959, E&S Ring began as a small family business...we never forgot our roots. Today, as a company with apartments throughout California, we still operate with all the thoughtfulness of a family-run establishment and we embrace our residents as part of our family circle. We strive to provide our residents with consistently exceptional customer service in memorable apartment home communities.

Greystar was founded in 1993 by Founder, Chairman, and CEO Bob Faith. Greystar is the global leader in rental housing with expertise in real estate sectors across multiple geographies. The company's business model is unique in its ability to own, operate, and develop collegiate, multifamily, corporate, and senior housing across the globe. Greystar continues to expand its geographic reach around the world, bringing a globally interconnected professional rental housing platform and industry funded with institutional capital to countries where the sector does not yet exist. With offices in more than 60 cities serving more than 200 markets globally, and more than 740,000 units and student beds under management, Greystar currently ranks first among the Top 50 US Apartment Managers according to the 2021 National Multifamily Housing Council. Greystar manages $41.3 billion in assets and oversees a global portfolio of more than 165,900 owned units across multiple strategies and geographies.

Since its inception in 1978, Worldwide Court Reporters has earned an unparalleled reputation for excellence in court reporting, videography, document databasing and trial support. Their cutting-edge technology has been utilized in many high-profile cases throughout the country and the globe providing live witness video and interactive real-time feed with available private chat. They are available 24/7 to assist with last-minute deposition scheduling or changes, and post-deposition details regardless of location. The status of all work is electronically tracked, utilizing the unique, customized software, ensuring that the answers to questions are always quickly accessible. Their services offered are court reporting, videographers, interpreters, deposition equipment, subpoena service, records retrieval, conference facilities, video conferencing, document management, trial presentation and support.

Farmers Insurance began in 1928 as the Farmers Automobile Inter-Insurance Exchange, created to serve drivers with affordable coverage. The company now offers insurance and financial products across home, auto, life, business, recreational vehicle, and device protection categories. Farmers Insurance uses a wide distribution model that includes exclusive agencies, independent agents, and direct sales channels, and it serves households and businesses across the United States.

Founded in 1991, JRK Property Holdings is a privately owned real estate investment and property management company headquartered in Los Angeles, California. The company was created with the purchase of five multifamily properties from an RTC pool of Executive Life assets that co-founder Jim Lippman had been managing via receivership. Jim Lippman currently serves as non-executive chairman, with the firm co-founded alongside Robert Rooney and Keith Holmes. As a privately held company, JRK has no ticker symbol.

JRK's core business focus is the acquisition, ownership, and operation of multifamily apartment communities, supplemented by a hotel division and a smaller commercial holdings segment. The firm pursues value-add and core-plus investment strategies. It operates two primary vehicles: its $1 billion Platform 5 Fund, which targets apartment assets built after 1990, and its MF Opportunities III fund, which targets vintage properties built in or before 1989. The company's asset classes of interest span multifamily (its primary focus), hospitality/hotels, and commercial properties including office complexes, storage facilities, and industrial parks.

In 2025, JRK ranked as the 50th largest apartment owner in the United States per the National Multi Housing Council, with 26,938 units. The company's residential portfolio spans 28 states, giving it a nationally diversified footprint that reduces exposure to any single market. Its 2025 acquisitions concentrated in gateway metros including Los Angeles, Seattle, Washington D.C., and Hoboken. Top markets by recent deployment include Southern California (Los Angeles), the Pacific Northwest (Seattle), and Washington D.C. Because its multifamily cash flows are distributed across tens of thousands of individual residential leases, the company carries limited single-tenant concentration exposure.

Founded in 1958, The Finger Companies is an independent developer and operator focused on luxury multifamily housing. The company's core work centers on apartment development, construction, investment building, and long-term property management. Its portfolio includes luxury apartment communities across Houston, the Chicago area, and Raleigh, reflecting a regional presence in major U.S. housing markets. The business has built and managed a substantial body of residential units over time, while maintaining its focus on design, location, and service-oriented management.

Lincoln Property Company began in Dallas, Texas in 1965 and has grown into a commercial real estate firm focused on development, leasing, property management, investment, advisory, and asset solutions. The company works across office, industrial, retail, multifamily, and mixed-use properties, serving owners, investors, lenders, and occupiers of commercial space. Lincoln maintains a broad national and global market presence, with services that support development, repositioning, and ongoing property operations. The company's business spans both real estate services and investment activity, reflecting a long-running platform built around commercial property management and development.

Bell Partners is a privately held multifamily apartment investment and management company. Founded in 1976, Bell Partners is a Greensboro-based independent firm that specializes in investing in and managing multifamily rental properties and apartment homes across the United States. The firm operates a vertically integrated platform, and with approximately 1,800 associates and nine offices, Bell Partners offers an extensive full-service vertically integrated national platform with expertise in property management, acquisitions, construction, financing, accounting, risk management, and related support functions.

The company's investment strategy targets value-add apartment communities. The firm engages in the acquisition, financing, management, and disposition of value-add apartment communities in supply-constrained submarkets, near major infrastructure and employment centers. Its asset-class focus is exclusively multifamily rental housing. Led by a senior management team with an average of 27 years of experience, Bell Partners has invested throughout all phases of the real estate cycle and has completed almost US$12 billion of realized apartment transactions since 2002.

RPD CATALYST, LLC is a highly experienced privately owned firm that has a 21-year track record of investing in all forms of real estate throughout the country.  RPD specializes in value-add, opportunistic and niche-market investments in residential, office and retail properties. 

Between them, RPD’s founding co-owners, Scott Dew and Richard Pachulski, have over fifty years of experience investing in real estate.  RPD President and CEO Scott Dew previously was the Co-President of Rubin Pachulski Dew Properties, LP (now Rubin Pachulski Properties, LP) and, before that, a managing partner of a law firm specializing in corporate and real estate bankruptcies and reorganizations.  RPD Managing Director Richard Pachulski is also a founder and officer of Rubin Pachulski Properties, LP and of the national bankruptcy law firm of Pachulski, Stang, Ziehl, Jones & Weintraub, LLC.

Camden Property Trust is a publicly traded multifamily real estate investment trust focused on the ownership, management, development, and redevelopment of apartment communities across high-growth U.S. markets. Co-founded by Richard Campo and Keith Oden in 1982, the company went public in 1993 and has since become an S&P 500 component and one of the largest multifamily REITs in the United States. The company operates with a vertically integrated model, handling construction, leasing, maintenance, and resident services in-house rather than outsourcing to third-party managers.

Camden's portfolio is concentrated in Sun Belt and select Mid-Atlantic markets with strong employment growth, population migration, and household formation trends. Key markets include Houston, Dallas, Atlanta, Phoenix, Tampa, Washington DC, and Charlotte. The company primarily owns Class A and upper-tier Class B apartment communities positioned in suburban and urban-suburban locations. In February 2026, Camden announced plans to exit California entirely, selling 11 properties totaling approximately 3,600 units valued at $1.5 billion, with proceeds to be redeployed into higher-return Sun Belt markets where regulatory environments are more favorable.

The company pursues growth through three parallel pipelines: development of new communities, selective acquisitions of stabilized assets, and capital recycling through dispositions of older properties. Camden maintains a disciplined approach to market timing, having navigated the elevated multifamily supply deliveries of 2024 while positioning for improved fundamentals as new construction slows. The company's management team has exhibited exceptional continuity, with co-founders Campo and Oden leading strategy for over 40 years.

Westdale Real Estate Investment and Management (“Westdale”) is a national real estate investment and management company headquartered in Dallas with six regional offices throughout the country. They focus on acquiring, managing and developing investment opportunities, including multifamily, office, retail, mixed-use and debt pools.

Cyclone Anaya's bought by Houston-based Dhanani Group.

Cyclone Anaya started his professional wrestling career at age 17 when he became the Champion of Mexico. Shortly thereafter, he came to the United States and made a dramatic entrance into the pro-wrestling circuit. Cyclone Anaya was a superb wrestler and won numerous awards and thrilled the hearts of millions of fans. He was indeed a Legend! During this time he met his wife of over 50 years, Carolina – a former Miss Houston. After many championship titles and five children, Cyclone and his family entered the restaurant business in Houston. After 50 years Cyclone Anaya’s has become a Texas legacy, serving Carolina’s original homemade recipes. Now the family is keeping the tradition alive and giving Texas and the nation the taste of fine homemade Mexican food that has made Cyclone Anaya’s famous.

Amegy Bank began in 1990 when Walter Johnson helped establish a Texas bank built around local relationships and community service. The company now operates as a full-service financial institution offering personal banking, commercial banking, digital banking, home loans, credit cards, foreign exchange solutions, and treasury management services. Amegy Bank also emphasizes a community bank partnership approach and serves Texans through banking centers in Houston, Central Texas, and the Dallas-Fort Worth region. The company was previously known as Southwest Bank of Texas.

Winther Investment, Inc., an upscale multifamily lifestyle development company, is privately held and headquartered in Houston, Texas.
