profile.locationBio: Marvell began in 1995 as a semiconductor company focused on digital storage, and the business has since expanded into a broader data infrastructure provider. The company develops networking, accelerated compute, storage, security, and custom silicon solutions for AI, cloud, carrier, and enterprise infrastructure, with a portfolio aimed at moving, storing, processing, and securing data. Marvell serves infrastructure customers across compute, connectivity, and storage markets and maintains a significant presence in semiconductors through products built for modern data centers and related systems.

Faegre Drinker is a multinational law firm offering a broad range of legal services to businesses, government entities, and nonprofit organizations. The firm was formed through the 2020 merger of Faegre Baker Daniels and Drinker Biddle & Reath, combining deep experience in litigation, regulatory, and transactional matters. Its practice areas include corporate law, intellectual property, labor and employment, product liability, real estate, and financial services. Faegre Drinker serves clients in sectors such as healthcare, insurance, technology, and manufacturing, providing strategic counsel on complex legal and business challenges. The firm operates from offices across the United States, as well as international locations, enabling it to support clients with cross-border transactions and global compliance issues. Headquartered in Philadelphia, the firm emphasizes innovation and client-focused solutions while maintaining a strong presence in key business and regulatory markets.

A member of the Mercury Aviation family, Mercury Fuels is backed by 60 years of excellence in the aviation industry.  Having been in the corporate and private aviation fuel business since 1996, Mercury Fuels maintains well-established relationships with FBOs and fuel suppliers that contribute to our great prices and service.

Integrity, customer loyalty, and industry leadership are the hallmarks of Mercury Fuels' offering in corporate aviation. No other company has sold as much fuel to fractional operators over the last two decades.

Mercury Fuels' customer list reads like a “who’s who” of U.S. and international aviation companies, while they strives to always offer the best possible prices and customer service.  With a network of hundreds of third-party fuel supply locations in the U.S. and over 1,000 international locations MercFuel provides comprehensive discount pricing and payment terms to all types of aviation customers.

Baylor College of Medicine began in Dallas in 1900 as the University of Dallas Medical Department and later affiliated with Baylor University, becoming Baylor University College of Medicine. The college later moved to Houston in the 1940s and became part of the Texas Medical Center, which shaped its growth in medical education and clinical work. Baylor College of Medicine today describes itself as a health sciences university that creates knowledge and applies science and discoveries to advance education, healthcare, and community service locally and globally. Its programs span medical education, graduate and health professions training, biomedical research, and patient care through a broad academic and clinical network.

AT&T began in 1885 as the American Telephone and Telegraph Company, a name now shortened to the AT&T brand. The company's roots trace to the early telephone era, and its modern business centers on wireless service, broadband, fiber, and business connectivity solutions. AT&T serves consumers and organizations with mobile plans, internet access, network services, and related digital tools, while also maintaining a significant presence in enterprise communications. The company has remained tied to major shifts in communications technology, moving from long-distance telephone networks into today's mix of wireless, broadband, and business services.

British Airways began in the nineteen seventies through the merger of major UK state-owned carriers, while its heritage traces back to early international air services and a long British aviation history. The airline operates as a full-service global airline with an extensive route network and a market presence spanning Europe, North America, South America, Asia, Africa and Australia. British Airways offers travel classes, booking and check-in tools, baggage information, airport guidance, holiday bookings, a loyalty programme, and Avios-based services for frequent travellers. The airline remains one of the best-known British carriers and continues to position itself as a global airline linking Britain with destinations worldwide.

PNC Mortgage provides comprehensive home lending services, including origination, refinancing, and loan servicing. As part of PNC Bank, it leverages a nationwide network of branches and mortgage offices to deliver competitive products and personalized solutions for homebuyers and homeowners. The division emphasizes efficiency, digital tools, and customer support to simplify the mortgage process.

ADT began in 1874 as American District Telegraph, growing from a telegraph-based call-box system into a business focused on protecting homes and commercial properties. The company now offers residential and small business security, interactive services, smart home solutions, fire protection, and alarm monitoring. ADT's history includes early work in central monitoring and automated alarm systems, which helped shape its long-running presence in the security industry. The company serves a broad U.S. customer base and maintains a large network supporting security and monitoring services.

Shorenstein is a privately owned real estate investment company headquartered in San Francisco that acquires, repositions, develops and operates office and mixed-use properties across the United States. Its roots trace to 1946, when Walter Shorenstein joined the brokerage Milton Meyer & Company. He became sole owner in 1960, renamed the firm and grew it into an owner and operator of San Francisco office buildings. His son, Douglas Shorenstein, became chairman and CEO in 1995 and expanded the company into a national investment, development and management platform. Brandon Shorenstein, Douglas's son, has led the firm as chairman and CEO since 2020 and also oversees the office portfolio owned by the Shorenstein family.

Capital is raised mainly through its Shorenstein Realty Investors closed-end funds, which Shorenstein Investment Advisers manages. An affiliate, Shorenstein Realty Services, provides asset management, leasing, property management and construction services. Since 1992, the firm and its affiliates have acquired $20.6 billion in assets, and they had 11.3 million square feet under management as of June 30, 2026. Investments include ground-up development, repositioning and stabilized assets, using direct acquisitions, mezzanine loans, preferred equity and joint ventures.

Recent buying has focused on leased office buildings with tenant amenities in submarkets with little new supply. Since June 2024, Shorenstein has acquired 14 office properties totaling approximately $2 billion. These include four Dallas-area assets, among them Sherry Lane Place and The Sterling in Preston Center, as well as two Nashville towers, Park Place at Bay Meadows in San Mateo and 901 K in Washington, D.C. The last purchase was 148 Lafayette in Manhattan's SoHo, the final investment for its Fund Fourteen. The firm still holds older properties in the Portland metro area, Philadelphia, New York, Charlotte and South Florida. It also has interests in The Spring District in Bellevue, which it co-developed with Wright Runstad & Company and where Meta leases office space.

In 1980, Nancy G. Brinker promised her dying sister, Susan, that she would do everything in her power to end breast cancer forever. In 1982, that promise became the Susan G. Komen® organization and the beginning of a global movement. What was started with $200 and a shoebox full of potential donor names has now grown into the world’s largest nonprofit source of funding for the fight against breast cancer. To date, they’ve invested more than $2.9 billion in groundbreaking research, community health outreach, advocacy and programs in more than 60 countries. Their efforts helped reduce deaths from breast cancer by 40 percent between 1989-2016 and we won’t stop until their promise is fulfilled.

profile.locationBio: Ricoh began in 1936 as a spin-off from the sensitized paper division of Rikagaku Kogyo and grew from early imaging roots into a global business technology company. The company's business domains include digital services, digital products, graphic communications, and industrial solutions, covering multifunction printers, printers, scanners, network equipment, software, and industrial printing systems. Ricoh also serves workplaces with applications, support, and service solutions, and its operations reach customers across a broad international network.

The Iris Cantor - UCLA Women's Health Education & Resource Center Mission

To provide comprehensive, exemplary health education programs to women and their loved ones that inform, support, and empower women to achieve their optimal level of health.

UCLA is recognized as a model for women's health care, uniting research, clinical care, medical training, public health education, and the promotion of women professionals around a common mission-to improve the health of diverse women across the life span.

Verizon began in 2000 through the merger of Bell Atlantic and GTE, forming a communications company that has since expanded beyond traditional telecom services. The company provides wireless connectivity, broadband, and fiber-based services for consumers and businesses, along with network and security solutions for enterprise customers. Verizon serves public-sector and large business customers through its Verizon Business unit, reflecting a broad mix of consumer, business, and network offerings. The company is a global communications technology company with a large market presence across mobility and broadband.

Volkert began in 1925 in New Orleans as Doullut & Ewin, later became Ewin Engineering, and eventually took the Volkert name after an engineer acquired the firm and shaped its long-term direction. The company is a professional services firm that provides planning, engineering, and construction services for public and private clients. Its work spans transportation infrastructure, environmental studies and permitting, program and construction management, construction engineering and inspection, and related infrastructure delivery services. Volkert serves a broad mix of markets, including municipalities, government, private development, environment, and transportation projects across the United States.

Extreme Networks began in 1996 in California, created by Gordon Stitt, Herb Schneider, and Stephen Haddock. The company provides networking hardware, software, and services for network management, security, and analytics. It serves diverse industries including healthcare, education, and hospitality. Over the years, Extreme Networks expanded through acquisitions like Enterasys Networks and Avaya's networking business. The company now offers cloud-managed solutions and has a global market presence.

Established in 1969, Moody Rambin specializes in providing project leasing, tenant representation, disposition, development, consulting, and management services to owners and tenants throughout the Texas region and the United States. As Houston’s largest locally owned, full-service commercial real estate brokerage and management firm, they believe that business is built on relationships. That’s why honesty and integrity are at the heart of everything they do.

Wells Fargo began in 1852 as a bank and express company serving the needs of the California Gold Rush and later evolved into a full-service financial institution. The company now offers consumer banking, commercial banking, corporate and investment banking, and wealth and investment management, with products that include deposit accounts, lending, mortgages, credit cards, treasury management, and investing services. Wells Fargo maintains a broad national and global business presence built through years of expansion and mergers, while continuing to emphasize financial services for households, businesses, and communities.

Travel Leaders Network formed in 2016 through the combination of Vacation.com, Results! Travel, and Travel Leaders Franchise Group, and later became part of Internova Travel Group. The company operates as a travel agency network serving leisure and corporate travel, with booking tools, marketing programs, lead-generation support, training, and supplier partnership programs for member agencies. Travel Leaders Network also supports consumer trip planning through TravelLeaders.com, connecting travelers with professional travel advisors across North America. The network has experienced continued member growth and renewed demand for consortium benefits, including technology, partner access, and agency support resources.

Livestream a place to broadcast live events, broadcast to millions, live in HD with our Platform, Producer, Broadcaster and Studio products.To enable organizations to share experiences through live video, unlocking a world where every event is available live online.

Salas O'Brien began in 1975 and has grown into an employee-owned engineering and technical services firm focused on advancing the human experience through the built environment. The firm provides a broad mix of engineering and technical consulting services for government and private sector clients, with work spanning the built environment, energy and resiliency, process design and integration, digital systems, sustainability consulting and design, and forensic consulting. Salas O'Brien also describes its business around helping clients adapt to changing conditions through integrated solutions that support long-term value. The company continues to expand through a wide North American network and added capabilities in multiple technical and industrial market areas through recent combinations with other firms.

John Hancock began in 1862 as a life insurer and later expanded into broader financial services. The company offers life insurance, long-term care insurance, mutual funds, annuities, retirement plan services, college savings plans, and investment solutions for individuals, families, businesses, and retirement plan participants. John Hancock operates as part of Manulife and maintains a broad presence in the U.S. financial services market through insurance, investing, retirement, and advice-oriented offerings, including its Vitality wellness-linked insurance program.

Mainfreight began operations in Auckland, New Zealand, in 1978 and has grown from a transport business into a global supply chain company. The company provides transport, air and ocean freight, warehousing, and end-to-end supply chain logistics solutions. Mainfreight now operates across Asia, Europe, Australia, New Zealand, and the Americas, supporting customers through a connected freight and distribution network.

Tangram Interiors is a workplace interiors firm that traces its roots to 1963 and focuses on commercial furniture, workplace design, space planning, AV technology, and installation services. Tangram Interiors serves corporate, healthcare, higher education, and K-12 environments, and the company also works across professional services projects with contract furniture, architectural wall systems, move and facility services, and custom studio solutions. Tangram Interiors operates as a Steelcase Premier Partner and maintains a broad portfolio of workplace projects and showroom-based support for organizations seeking coordinated interior solutions.

ADT began in 1874 as American District Telegraph, growing from a telegraph-based call-box system into a business focused on protecting homes and commercial properties. The company now offers residential and small business security, interactive services, smart home solutions, fire protection, and alarm monitoring. ADT's history includes early work in central monitoring and automated alarm systems, which helped shape its long-running presence in the security industry. The company serves a broad U.S. customer base and maintains a large network supporting security and monitoring services.

Alcoholics Anonymous is a fellowship of people who come together to address drinking problems and pursue sobriety through mutual support and the Twelve Steps. The organization began in 1935 after a meeting between Bill W. and Dr. Bob, and early groups in Ohio and New York helped shape the fellowship's growth. Regular meetings, peer sharing, anonymity, and service form the core of the recovery approach. Alcoholics Anonymous provides information and educational materials for the public and for professionals who work with people affected by alcohol use.

MD Anderson Cancer Center was founded in 1941 as a Texas cancer hospital and research program, later becoming part of The University of Texas System. The cancer center focuses on patient care, cancer research, prevention, and education, with services spanning diagnosis, treatment, clinical research, and survivorship support. MD Anderson Cancer Center serves patients from across the United States and around the world and remains closely identified with cancer specialty care and translational research. The institution's mission centers on eliminating cancer through integrated programs in care, research, prevention, and training.

Old Republic National Title Insurance Company is part of Old Republic Title, a business founded in 1907 that provides title insurance and settlement services for real estate transactions. The company serves homeowners, lenders, real estate professionals, title agents, and commercial clients through a national network of company-owned offices, affiliates, authorized agents, and approved attorneys. Its offerings include escrow and closing support, commercial title insurance services, and agency solutions for title agents. Old Republic Title is a wholly owned subsidiary of Old Republic International Corporation and operates as one of the larger title insurance groups in the United States.

Any Lab Test Now began in 1992 and debuted as a franchise concept in 2007. The company provides direct access to clinical, DNA, and drug and alcohol lab testing services, along with phlebotomy and specimen collection services, through a retail storefront model. Customers include consumers, businesses, and government entities, and the business is built around walk-in testing, upfront pricing, and fast turnaround for many results. Any Lab Test Now operates as a franchise system with independently owned and operated store locations across the United States. The company also supports business testing needs, including workplace-related testing and other compliance-focused services.

Buildingstars of Phoenix specializes in delivering commercial cleaning and janitorial services to businesses across the Phoenix metropolitan area. The company operates as part of the Buildingstars franchise network, which was founded in 1994 by Chris Blase in St. Louis, Missouri. Its core offerings include routine office cleaning, floor care, and restroom sanitation, with an emphasis on maintaining healthy and professional work environments. Buildingstars serves a range of industries, including corporate offices, healthcare facilities, and educational institutions, tailoring its services to meet specific client needs. The organization is privately held and operates through a franchise model, allowing local ownership while maintaining standardized service quality. Over the years, Buildingstars has expanded its footprint across multiple U.S. markets, positioning itself as a recognized provider in the janitorial services sector.

Founded in 1980, Fentress Studios is a global design firm headquartered in Denver with five studios located throughout the United States. Their talented team of professionals have designed more than $52 billion in architectural landmarks worldwide, which have garnered close to 700 awards and are visited by more than 750 million people each year.
Their firm is internationally known for innovative, award-winning design of public buildings, including airports, museums, convention centers, civic and judicial facilities, laboratories, higher education, and more. Their portfolio also includes office, mixed-use, high rise, worship, and residential buildings.
They partner with their clients to deliver sustainability and resiliency, mission-critical technology, revitalization and transformation, historical preservation and restoration, studies and planning.

Kastle Systems has been a leader in the security industry since 1972, providing state-of-the-art managed security solutions that protect more than thousands of properties and  businesses across the United States and Australia. Kastle’s services include access control, video surveillance, visitor management, identity management, and more, all delivered through its innovative cloud-based platform. With a commitment to open architecture integration, cutting-edge technology, and comprehensive managed services, Kastle enables clients to achieve operational efficiency, scalability, and peace of mind without the burden of managing complex security systems. What makes Kastle exceptional is their focus on security as a managed service. It’s all they do, and all they've ever done. They have built their company on the belief that the most effective approach is a complete one: because they engineer, install, monitor, and maintain clients system, they are invested in its end-to-end performance.

The National Minority Supplier Development Council (NMSDC) began in 1972 as the National Minority Purchasing Council and later adopted its current name. NMSDC connects certified minority-owned businesses with corporate members, contracts, capital, education, and peer business opportunities through a market-based model built around certification and supplier development. The organization supports corporate members with tools for supplier diversity, regional affiliate networks, and programs that help minority business enterprises build capability and pursue larger business relationships. NMSDC functions as a national network focused on minority business inclusion, economic mobility, and supply-chain access across industries.

The company began in 1958 when Tom Cousins started a residential real estate business, and the firm later evolved from a Georgia homebuilder into a Sun Belt office REIT. The business develops, owns, and manages Class A office properties through a fully integrated real estate investment trust structure. Its portfolio is centered on trophy office assets in high-growth Sun Belt markets, with activity tied to development, acquisition, leasing, and property management.

Wells Fargo began in 1852 as a bank and express company serving the needs of the California Gold Rush and later evolved into a full-service financial institution. The company now offers consumer banking, commercial banking, corporate and investment banking, and wealth and investment management, with products that include deposit accounts, lending, mortgages, credit cards, treasury management, and investing services. Wells Fargo maintains a broad national and global business presence built through years of expansion and mergers, while continuing to emphasize financial services for households, businesses, and communities.

American Income Life Insurance Company began in 1951 when Bernard Rapoport founded the business with borrowed capital. The company focuses on life, accident, and supplemental health insurance for working families, with coverage tied to labor unions, credit unions, associations, and their families. American Income Life operates as an international insurer serving customers in the United States, Canada, and New Zealand, and it is part of Globe Life.

PwC is a British professional services network that provides audit, consulting, deals, and tax services for public and private clients. The company combines industry-focused capabilities with work in technology, risk, analytics, legal services, and financial advisory, serving organisations across a broad range of sectors. PwC traces its roots to London in the mid-19th century and later took shape through a merger of major accounting firms, giving the business a long history in client service and assurance. The firm maintains a significant global presence and continues to organize its work around trust, transformation, and problem-solving for clients in the UK and beyond.

Corporate Finance Associates began in 1956 as a middle-market advisory firm focused on mergers and acquisitions and related capital needs. The company works with business owners on sell-side advisory, buy-side advisory, recapitalizations, divestitures, acquisition financing, and broader corporate finance assignments. Corporate Finance Associates also covers debt and equity capital markets, serving clients across many industries through an international network of offices in the Americas, Europe, and Asia. The firm emphasizes independent, senior-led guidance for business sales, acquisitions, growth capital, and restructuring needs.

profile.locationBio: Fragomen was established in 1951 and grew from a U.S. immigration law practice into a global immigration services firm. The company focuses on business immigration, visa and work permit support, immigration compliance, and mobility planning for organizations operating across borders. Fragomen also provides advisory services for private clients, including residency and citizenship planning, alongside support for families and individuals navigating cross-border relocation. Its work spans a wide range of industries and jurisdictions, reflecting a market presence built around immigration matters rather than broader general legal practice.

profile.locationBio: Numotion serves individuals with mobility limitations through specialized products and services. Established in 2001 and headquartered in Tennessee, the company provides customized wheelchairs and assistive technologies. Their offerings include complex rehabilitation technology and home medical equipment. Numotion operates numerous branches nationwide while maintaining a focus on personalized service. The company partners with healthcare providers to deliver tailored mobility solutions that enhance users' independence.

Sun Life began in 1865 in Montreal as The Sun Insurance Company of Montreal and later became Sun Life Assurance Company of Canada. The company has grown into a Canadian-based international financial services business focused on insurance, wealth solutions, asset management, and customized health programs. Sun Life serves individuals, employers, and institutional clients through life, health, and travel insurance, savings and investment products, pension and benefit solutions, and specialized financial protection services. The company continues to operate across Canada and other major markets as part of a diversified financial services group with a long history in protection and wealth management.

DeHay & Elliston began in 1992 and traces its roots through the career of J. Carlisle DeHay, Jr., who practiced in Dallas County for more than four decades. The firm operates as a litigation practice with a broad civil defense focus, including medical malpractice, personal injury, toxic torts, professional liability, products liability, premises liability, and insurance defense. The company also handles general civil and business matters, along with banking, corporate, commercial transactions, real estate, and sports law. DeHay & Elliston serves clients through a multi-office presence and continues to center its work on trial and litigation services.

ERM was formed in 1987 through the merger of two earlier environmental consultancies, building on roots that date back to 1971. The company provides environmental, health, safety, risk, social and sustainability consulting, with work spanning climate, net zero, reporting, disclosure and business transformation. ERM offers digital and advisory solutions that help organisations measure progress, manage sustainability challenges and adapt strategy across changing regulatory and market conditions. ERM serves a broad international client base and remains focused on sustainability as its core business.

Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) was founded in 2000 to digitize the energy markets and provide greater price transparency. They have been transforming markets, products and processes ever since. By combining their world class technology with their leading data services and operating expertise, ICE adds transparency and enables customer efficiency gains that advance both their networks and solutions for their customers.

Altegra Health™ is a national vendor of technology-enabled, end-to-end payment solutions providing health plans and other risk-bearing organizations with the data they need to expertly manage member care and ensure appropriate reimbursement.

The power of Altegra Health’s advanced analytics and supporting interventions enables healthcare organizations to elevate care quality, optimize financial performance, and enhance the member experience.

Heights Wellness Retreat began in 2004 as Massage Heights and later evolved into a hybrid, membership-based wellness brand centered on recovery, restoration, and everyday longevity. The company offers massage therapy, skincare, meditation, and touchless wellness services that are designed to fit into recurring wellness routines. Heights Wellness Retreat operates as a franchised wellness system with a broad market presence across the United States, and the brand has positioned itself around integrated service paths that combine hands-on care with recovery technologies.

Royal Prestige began as part of Hy Cite Enterprises, which was founded in 1959 by Peter O. Johnson, and the brand later developed into a premium kitchenware line. The company focuses on cookware, tableware, and related home kitchen products, and its business model centers on independent authorized distributors, customer support, and financing options. Royal Prestige describes its products as durable cookware designed for home use, and the business continues to serve a broad market through direct selling and branded product offerings.

Earthbar started in 1971 as Great Earth Vitamins, a health food pioneer. The brand evolved into a full wellness destination around 2009 when the company added juice bars to its retail locations. Now operating under the Earthbar name, the company serves health-conscious consumers through numerous California and New York locations. Offerings include made-to-order smoothies, superfood bowls, supplements, and grab-and-go items. The business partners with fitness centers like Equinox for in-club locations. Earthbar emphasizes premium nutrition and holistic wellness through curated products and educational resources.

Avaya began as a spin-off from Lucent Technologies in 2000 and has since developed into an enterprise communications software company. The company provides hybrid cloud contact center services, unified communications, and collaboration offerings designed to connect voice, digital channels, insights, and workflows for large organizations. Avaya serves customers across industries including financial services, healthcare, airlines, and pharmaceuticals, and its product portfolio centers on customer experience and enterprise communications.

Greycourt is an independent investment advisory firm founded in 1988. The company began with a focus on serving sophisticated investors and has grown into an open-architecture advisory business that avoids product sales in favor of advice. Greycourt provides customized portfolio design, asset allocation, manager research, and related investment support for ultra-high-net-worth families, family offices, and select institutions. The firm also offers co-sourced advisory services that combine personalized planning with ongoing research and portfolio oversight. Greycourt maintains a market presence across several U.S. cities and continues to expand its advisory and research capabilities.

DHR Global began in 1989 as a retained executive search firm and later expanded through Jobplex into emerging leader search. The company now provides executive search, board and CEO search, leadership consulting, assessments, coaching, succession planning, and organizational development for clients across global markets. DHR Global serves organizations across many industries and maintains a broad international footprint while keeping a boutique-style service model.

Imperial PFS began in 1977 as Premium Financing Specialists, later merging with Imperial Credit Corporation to form the current business under the Imperial PFS brand. The company provides commercial premium financing and payment technology for insurance agents, brokers, carriers, policyholders, and business owners, with services that support premium payments, cash flow, and digital document and payment workflows. Imperial PFS has grown into one of the largest premium financing providers in North America and maintains a broad market presence across the United States, Canada, and Puerto Rico.

L3Harris Technologies was formed in 2019 through the merger of Harris Corporation and L3 Technologies, bringing together two long-running defense and technology businesses. The company develops mission-critical solutions for customers across air, land, sea, space, and cyber domains, with work spanning command and control systems, communications, tactical radios, avionics, electronic systems, and intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance capabilities. L3Harris Technologies serves commercial and government markets through its aerospace and defense portfolio, and the company organizes its work across three strategic business segments: Space & Mission Systems, Communications & Spectrum Dominance, and Missile Solutions. L3Harris Technologies maintains a significant global presence with a broad international operating footprint across multiple countries.

Graham Holdings Company began as The Washington Post in 1877 and later evolved into a diversified holding company. The company operates across educational services, home health and hospice care, television broadcasting, online, print and local TV news, automotive dealerships, manufacturing, hospitality, and consumer internet businesses. Its portfolio reflects a long transition from newspaper roots into a broader mix of service and media-related businesses, with Kaplan among the better-known parts of the business. The company maintains a significant market presence through multiple operating segments and a varied set of consumer and business services.

DSV began in 1976 when Leif Tullberg and nine independent trucking companies established the business in Denmark. The company grew from contract haulage into a global transport and logistics group through acquisitions that expanded road, air, sea, and contract logistics capabilities. The company offers freight forwarding, road freight, air freight, sea freight, contract logistics, and digital tools for booking, tracking, warehouse management, and supply-chain control. A recent acquisition of Schenker expanded the company's global network and added to its broad international market presence.

The company produces and distributes industrial and medical gases together with related equipment and services, and its activities are organised around engineering and technologies, large industries, industrial merchant, healthcare, and electronics. Air Liquide supports sectors ranging from energy and chemicals to hospitals, semiconductor manufacturing and scientific research, with a broad international presence and a long-established role in essential molecules and process solutions. The business also places emphasis on hydrogen, healthcare services and industrial decarbonisation as part of its current market activity.

Federal Aviation Administration began in 1958 as the Federal Aviation Agency and later adopted its current name after joining the U.S. Department of Transportation in 1967. The agency regulates and oversees civil aviation, including air traffic control, aircraft and personnel certification, airport standards, and safety rules for the national airspace system. FAA also handles related functions such as aircraft registration, aeronautical charts, airways information, aviation insurance, and commercial space transportation oversight. The organization serves as the federal authority for managing U.S. skies and maintaining aviation safety and efficiency across the system.

RPM is an Austin, Texas-based multifamily property owner-operator, investment, and development firm active across the United States. Founded in 2002 as Roscoe Property Management by Jason Berkowitz, the company began with just 10 units under management. Through both organic growth and strategic mergers, RPM Living has evolved into one of the nation's largest multifamily operators. 

The firm manages 226,169 units across 26 states. RPM operates through a vertically integrated platform encompassing property management, investment acquisitions, and development. The company maintains 12 regional offices. In 2021, RPM merged with Atlanta-based CF Real Estate Services, expanding its footprint across the Southeast and Midwest. This transaction added approximately 26,000 units to the portfolio. The merger with CF Real Estate Services brought together leadership from both organizations under the RPM brand.

Murphy's Deli is a deli chain with a broad menu that includes breakfast items, sandwiches, wraps, salads, pitas, burgers, and Mediterranean-style specialties. The company provides catering for office meals and events, with customizable options centered on deli platters and tray offerings. Its location network spans multiple Texas markets, including several Houston-area sites and other Texas cities, supporting both dine-in and order-ahead service. The company operates as a neighborhood deli concept built around fresh prepared food and convenience for everyday meals and group orders.

Ledgent Finance & Accounting, formerly Ledgent Search Group, is a specialized business line of Roth Staffing Companies that focuses on finance and accounting staffing. Ledgent Finance & Accounting places accounting and finance talent across temporary, temp-to-hire, direct hire, executive search, and large-scale staffing assignments, and it serves job seekers and employers across the U.S. The company offers roles such as accountants, bookkeepers, controllers, payroll professionals, and financial leaders, with support for both remote and on-site hiring needs.

Lexmark began in 1991 as a spin-off of IBM and built its business around imaging and output technology. Lexmark serves customers across industries such as manufacturing, retail, financial services, healthcare, education, and government, with products and services sold in many markets worldwide. In 2025, Xerox completed its acquisition of Lexmark, and Lexmark now operates as part of Xerox while continuing its imaging and print-services focus.

RemX is the professional staffing division of EmployBridge and serves employers and job seekers through temporary, temp-to-hire, direct hire, independent contract, executive search, managed staffing, and outsourced workforce solutions. A brand refresh in 2017 marked a new chapter for RemX, while the company continued to position itself around specialized recruiting and matching talent with roles that fit specific skill sets. RemX focuses on business verticals that include accounting and finance, contact center solutions, healthcare, legal, professional business operations and support, and information technology, with healthcare staffing extending from medical billing and coding to physician-level roles.

Spectrum is the consumer brand of Charter Communications, a cable company founded in 1993 that launched Spectrum as its market name in 2014, replacing earlier Charter-branded services. Happy Home Communities is a manufactured housing and RV community investment platform launched by Gelt in 2017 to acquire, improve, and operate mobile home parks and RV resorts. Formed as an extension of Gelt’s private real estate investment activities, the platform focused initially on value-add acquisitions—bringing in-fill homes to vacant pads, upgrading common areas, and professionalizing on-site operations to enhance stabilized cash flow. The inaugural purchase was De Rancho Y Mobile Villa, a nine-acre, 90-space mobile home community in Bakersfield, California. Later in 2017, Happy Home Communities acquired a three-property, 439-space portfolio in Pennsylvania, with planned amenity upgrades and in-fill on vacant lots over a multi-year hold.

Strategically, the platform targeted manufactured housing and RV communities—assets with historically resilient occupancy, diversified resident bases (lot renters typically own their homes), and opportunities to drive NOI through low-capital operational improvements compared with conventional multifamily. Over its early life, the program assembled a portfolio that—per leadership bios subsequently published—grew to eight properties and was later sold as a portfolio, indicating an opportunistic strategy cycle rather than permanent-hold ownership.

Top market exposure historically included Bakersfield, California and, in Pennsylvania, the Scranton–Wilkes-Barre metro (Exeter), Williamsport (Muncy), and Selinsgrove. Based on publicly reported acquisitions, Pennsylvania accounted for the majority of known homesites (approximately 439 of 529, or ~83%). As a manufactured housing operator, the rent roll is broadly distributed across individual households; there are no single corporate tenants. The platform is privately held; there is no public ticker.

In 1981, Siegi Izakson, a Holocaust survivor and long-time Houston resident, had an epiphany. After attending an international gathering of Holocaust survivors in Israel, Izakson realized his peers were getting older, and as they passed away their stories and memories of unchecked prejudice would go with them. He returned to Houston, convinced that the city needed a Holocaust education center and memorial that would preserve for future generations the memory of those who had perished and the stories of those who had survived.

The firm also invests in hospitality, retail and mixed-use assets. It lends against office, multifamily, industrial and hospitality properties.

At year-end 2025, the company's own net lease portfolio had 202 properties totaling 6.7 million square feet in 37 states. The largest state exposures by annualized rental income were Virginia (16%), Ohio (12%) and Wisconsin (8%). Four tenants made up 28% of annualized rental income: CVS (9%), Cabela's (7%), United Oil (6%) and Lowe's (6%). Camden Property Trust is a publicly traded multifamily real estate investment trust focused on the ownership, management, development, and redevelopment of apartment communities across high-growth U.S. markets. Co-founded by Richard Campo and Keith Oden in 1982, the company went public in 1993 and has since become an S&P 500 component and one of the largest multifamily REITs in the United States. The company operates with a vertically integrated model, handling construction, leasing, maintenance, and resident services in-house rather than outsourcing to third-party managers.

Camden's portfolio is concentrated in Sun Belt and select Mid-Atlantic markets with strong employment growth, population migration, and household formation trends. Key markets include Houston, Dallas, Atlanta, Phoenix, Tampa, Washington DC, and Charlotte. The company primarily owns Class A and upper-tier Class B apartment communities positioned in suburban and urban-suburban locations. In February 2026, Camden announced plans to exit California entirely, selling 11 properties totaling approximately 3,600 units valued at $1.5 billion, with proceeds to be redeployed into higher-return Sun Belt markets where regulatory environments are more favorable.

The company pursues growth through three parallel pipelines: development of new communities, selective acquisitions of stabilized assets, and capital recycling through dispositions of older properties. Camden maintains a disciplined approach to market timing, having navigated the elevated multifamily supply deliveries of 2024 while positioning for improved fundamentals as new construction slows. The company's management team has exhibited exceptional continuity, with co-founders Campo and Oden leading strategy for over 40 years.

Silixa is a United Kingdom–based technology company specializing in distributed fibre-optic sensing systems used to monitor assets and environments in real time. Founded in 2007, the company develops and deploys distributed acoustic, temperature, and strain sensing technologies that convert standard fibre-optic cables into continuous sensor arrays. These systems are applied across sectors including energy, mining, infrastructure, environmental monitoring, carbon capture and storage, and defense.
Silixa’s technology enables high-resolution data acquisition over long distances and in harsh operating environments, supporting applications such as subsurface monitoring, pipeline surveillance, asset integrity assessment, and process optimization. The company operates globally, with technical and operational activities in Europe and North America, and provides both hardware systems and associated data and engineering services. Silixa has been recognized for its technical innovation through industry awards and participation in government- and defense-related technology programs.
In December 2023, Silixa was acquired by Luna Innovations, expanding its role within a broader sensing and instrumentation platform while continuing to operate under the Silixa name. The company remains privately operated within the Luna corporate structure.

The company focuses on in-house design, engineering, manufacturing, and testing of radiation detection components, supporting both standard product offerings and custom detector configurations. Global Nucleonics’ technical heritage traces back several decades through predecessor organizations involved in nuclear and radiation detection technologies. Its detectors are used across markets such as oilfield services, nuclear power, medical instrumentation, homeland security, and scientific research.
Global Nucleonics maintains ISO 9001 certification and is led by technical management with prior experience in international radiation detection and instrumentation firms. The company remains privately held and operates from its Houston headquarters.

Founded in 1991, JRK Property Holdings is a privately owned real estate investment and property management company headquartered in Los Angeles, California. The company was created with the purchase of five multifamily properties from an RTC pool of Executive Life assets that co-founder Jim Lippman had been managing via receivership. Jim Lippman currently serves as non-executive chairman, with the firm co-founded alongside Robert Rooney and Keith Holmes. As a privately held company, JRK has no ticker symbol.

JRK's core business focus is the acquisition, ownership, and operation of multifamily apartment communities, supplemented by a hotel division and a smaller commercial holdings segment. The firm pursues value-add and core-plus investment strategies. It operates two primary vehicles: its $1 billion Platform 5 Fund, which targets apartment assets built after 1990, and its MF Opportunities III fund, which targets vintage properties built in or before 1989. The company's asset classes of interest span multifamily (its primary focus), hospitality/hotels, and commercial properties including office complexes, storage facilities, and industrial parks.

In 2025, JRK ranked as the 50th largest apartment owner in the United States per the National Multi Housing Council, with 26,938 units. The company's residential portfolio spans 28 states, giving it a nationally diversified footprint that reduces exposure to any single market. Its 2025 acquisitions concentrated in gateway metros including Los Angeles, Seattle, Washington D.C., and Hoboken. Top markets by recent deployment include Southern California (Los Angeles), the Pacific Northwest (Seattle), and Washington D.C. Because its multifamily cash flows are distributed across tens of thousands of individual residential leases, the company carries limited single-tenant concentration exposure.

Since inception, Hanover has developed over $18 billion in total projects, including more than 70,000 multifamily units and 14 million square feet of industrial space. The company maintains in-house capabilities across development, design, construction, property management, capital markets, and legal functions. Hanover's portfolio spans 18 states and 33 cities, with a geographic concentration in Texas and California. California represents the firm's single-largest state exposure with 36 properties, followed by Texas. The company's top markets by property count include Austin (8 properties), Atlanta (7 properties), and Baltimore (5 properties). Hanover operates through approximately 60 holding entities and maintains lending relationships with Truist Bank, Wells Fargo Bank, and other institutional lenders. The property management division has maintained the highest online reputation score nationwide in the apartment management industry for three consecutive years. Leadership is led by founder Murry Bowden (Executive Chairman), with second-generation family members Brandt Bowden (CEO) and Jeb Bowden (COO) overseeing operations.

BOE Technology Group, founded in April 1993, is a publicly traded company headquartered in Beijing, China. The company specializes in semiconductor display technologies and IoT-based solutions for information interaction and healthcare. BOE operates through multiple business segments, including display devices, sensors, smart systems, and medical engineering. It is recognized as one of the world’s largest manufacturers of LCD and OLED panels, supplying displays for smartphones, tablets, laptops, monitors, and TVs. BOE has expanded globally with subsidiaries in over 20 countries and maintains a strong presence in advanced display technologies such as flexible AMOLED and Mini/Micro LED. Listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange under ticker 000725, BOE has consistently ranked among the top global patent filers and leads the industry in LCD panel shipments.

AMC is a multifamily property management firm that serves property owners, residents, and vendors through full-service management and asset-focused operations. The company was founded in 2000 and has built its business around managing apartment communities with an ownership mentality, operational discipline, financial oversight, and attention to long-term value. AMC operates in Utah as part of a broader national portfolio, reflecting a market presence centered on apartment property management rather than a single local market.

Niagen Bioscience began in 1999 as ChromaDex and later rebranded under its current name, building a business around NAD+ research and nicotinamide riboside science. The company develops consumer supplements, ingredient technology, and pharmaceutical-grade intravenous and injectable products through its Niagen platform, supported by clinical research, peer-reviewed publications, and a patent portfolio. Niagen Bioscience focuses on healthy-aging and cellular-health applications, with commercial activity centered on oral wellness products and clinical-use formats that extend the same ingredient science across multiple business verticals.

Based in Dallas, Steward + Helm is focused on delivering high quality apartment living experiences to working households by acquiring, improving and managing multifamily communities that have long suffered from neglect and underperformance. The strive to be good stewards of the communities thry operate, supported by mission-driven team members who take the helm to deliver great living experiences. Supported by more than 200 dedicated team members, Steward + Helm own and operate nearly 50 apartment communities in Alabama, Arkansas, Florida, Louisiana and Texas – all acquired since December 2019 in growing markets that need quality rental housing to support economic growth.

Flatbay Capital began in 2019 as a Texas-based private credit firm focused on owner-occupied commercial real estate financing. The company provides direct lending and bridge loan solutions for businesses that need short-term capital to refinance bank debt, support acquisitions or expansion, or unlock equity in commercial property. Its lending work centers on non-bank commercial real estate loans for business owners in transition, with structures designed to help borrowers move back toward traditional bank financing after a short period. The firm also works through referral relationships with bankers, lenders, and other deal sources as part of its market approach.

Huffman Builders has been engaged in real estate development, construction, and sales since the 1970’s. They excel in all aspects of specialty medical facilities and turnkey medical/professional offices. Huffman will find your site, coordinate architecture and engineering, construct your facility, and finance all interim costs for your new project. Huffman Builders also delivers innovative investment and brokerage services. Huffman Builders provides the most complete set of services in the industry.

Greystar was founded in 1993 by Founder, Chairman, and CEO Bob Faith. Greystar is the global leader in rental housing with expertise in real estate sectors across multiple geographies. The company's business model is unique in its ability to own, operate, and develop collegiate, multifamily, corporate, and senior housing across the globe. Greystar continues to expand its geographic reach around the world, bringing a globally interconnected professional rental housing platform and industry funded with institutional capital to countries where the sector does not yet exist. With offices in more than 60 cities serving more than 200 markets globally, and more than 740,000 units and student beds under management, Greystar currently ranks first among the Top 50 US Apartment Managers according to the 2021 National Multifamily Housing Council. Greystar manages $41.3 billion in assets and oversees a global portfolio of more than 165,900 owned units across multiple strategies and geographies.

California Landmark Group, formed in 1988, acquires, rehabilitates and develops real estate throughout California. Ford Motor Company began in 1903 and grew from early automobile production into a broad mobility business. The company now focuses on passenger vehicles, trucks, electric and hybrid models, performance vehicles, commercial vehicles, service and parts, connected services, and financing through Ford Credit. Ford maintains operations across North America and in worldwide markets, supporting vehicle shopping, purchase, and financing through its global network.

Honeywell began in 1885 with Albert Butz's furnace regulator invention, and the business later grew through the Honeywell Heating Specialty Co. and the Minneapolis-Honeywell Regulator Co. merger in the 1920s. The company now focuses on automation and related technology-led solutions for building, process, and industrial environments, with offerings tied to safety, productivity, efficiency, and uptime. Honeywell maintains a long history in industrial controls and mission-critical technologies, and operates today as a pure-play automation company with a long operating legacy.

DolEx Financial Services has built a consumer financial services business around money movement and everyday payment needs, with more than 20 years in the industry. DolEx operates as a financial institution and money services business, with bilingual customer support and both branch-based and digital access for customers.

ZRS Management began operations in 1991 as a multifamily property management firm. The company provides services including property operations, marketing, leasing, and accounting. ZRS serves institutional clients and individual owners while maintaining a focus on community management. Through strategic growth, the company has established a significant national footprint in the property management sector.

Second Home is a privately held workspace operator founded in 2014. It develops coworking environments designed to support creative work, entrepreneurship, and community engagement. The company first established its presence in London, where its Spitalfields site serves as a hub for workspace users seeking flexible office arrangements and access to meeting and cultural facilities. Second Home’s portfolio has expanded to additional locations, including West London and Lisbon, offering a consistent focus on design-led environments and communal amenities. The Dinerstein Companies is a privately held, vertically integrated real estate development, construction, and property management firm headquartered in Houston, Texas. Founded in 1955, the company has developed over 80,000 multifamily apartment units and 50,000 student housing beds across the United States over seven decades of operation. TDC manages $4.31 billion in assets and has delivered $5.30 billion in new developments since 2010. The firm operates as a full-service platform, maintaining in-house development, construction, property management, and design divisions. TDC's investment approach focuses on high-growth submarkets with employment drivers in medical, institutional, and educational sectors, emphasizing walkability and community connectivity in core locations. The company ranks as one of the nation's leading green developers, with over $4.7 billion in LEED and Fitwell certified product completed or under construction. TDC has established long-term partnerships with institutional capital providers, including Harrison Street Asset Management, with whom it has collaborated on 34 multifamily and student housing transactions since 2013. The firm's geographic footprint extends from Florida to California, targeting markets that align with its focus on quality, sustainability, and operational excellence.

Gables Residential is a privately held real estate investment trust and owner-operator headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia. Founded in 1982, the company operates as a vertically integrated platform focused on the development, construction, acquisition, and management of multifamily and mixed-use communities across high-growth U.S. markets. The firm owns and manages approximately 25,000 to 28,000 apartment homes and 750,000 square feet of retail space. In 2015, Clarion Partners led a consortium of 12 global institutional investors in a $3.2 billion acquisition and recapitalization of Gables, converting the company into an open-end fund structure with an initial portfolio of 54 luxury communities.
Gables operates in multiple markets including Atlanta, Austin, Boston, Dallas, Denver, Houston, Jacksonville, Orlando, Salt Lake City, Seattle, South Florida, Southern California, and metropolitan Washington, D.C. The company also provides third-party management services in Tampa, North Florida, Chicago, New York, and Phoenix. The portfolio includes both wholly-owned assets and third-party managed properties, with development projects underway in several key markets. As of August 2026, public records indicate 59 current property ownerships held through 32 confirmed entities, with $12.8 billion in total recorded mortgage volume across 161 mortgages.
The company employs over 900 associates and maintains an average employee tenure of 5.59 years. Gables' multifamily focus inherently diversifies tenant concentration risk across thousands of individual residential leases rather than reliance on a few corporate tenants. The firm has received national recognition for development excellence, property management, and sustainability practices, including multiple FGBC certifications and Fitwel ratings at various communities. Key geographic exposure includes concentrations in Texas markets (Dallas, Houston, Austin), Florida (South Florida, Orlando, Jacksonville, Tampa), and the Washington, D.C. metro area.

MRC Global began as McJunkin Supply Company in 1921 and later grew through a series of heritage businesses into MRC Global. The company distributes pipe, valves, fittings, and related infrastructure products and services for gas utilities, downstream, industrial, energy transition, pipeline, and transmission infrastructure markets. Its offering also includes technical support, quality programs, and supply-chain solutions built around complex industrial sourcing needs. In 2025, DNOW completed its acquisition of MRC Global, bringing the business into a broader energy and industrial distribution platform.

profile.locationBio: French and Spanish colonial governments depended on the Tunica for trade, diplomacy with other tribes, and as a barrier against British encroachment. The Spanish conquistador, Hernando de Soto, may have visited the ancestral Tunica town of Quizquiz in 1541, according to some archeologists. But the first documented contact with the Tunica Tribe was with French colonists in Louisiana. The tribe had shifted its location to a site near the mouth of the Yazoo River by 1694, when the French Jesuits established a mission under Father Antoine Daivon. As the southernmost Indian nation to oppose the English, the Tunica cultivated a relationship with France as early as 1699. Hatred of the English-inspired and English-armed Chickasaw slave traders brought the French and Tunica together and prompted the Tunica to move their village from the Yazoo River basin halfway to New Orleans.

Camden Property Trust is a publicly traded multifamily real estate investment trust focused on the ownership, management, development, and redevelopment of apartment communities across high-growth U.S. markets. The company operates with a vertically integrated model, handling construction, leasing, maintenance, and resident services in-house rather than outsourcing to third-party managers.

Camden's portfolio is concentrated in Sun Belt and select Mid-Atlantic markets with strong employment growth, population migration, and household formation trends. Key markets include Houston, Dallas, Atlanta, Phoenix, Tampa, Washington DC, and Charlotte. The company primarily owns Class A and upper-tier Class B apartment communities positioned in suburban and urban-suburban locations. In February 2026, Camden announced plans to exit California entirely, selling 11 properties totaling approximately 3,600 units valued at $1.5 billion, with proceeds to be redeployed into higher-return Sun Belt markets where regulatory environments are more favorable.

The company pursues growth through three parallel pipelines: development of new communities, selective acquisitions of stabilized assets, and capital recycling through dispositions of older properties. Camden maintains a disciplined approach to market timing, having navigated the elevated multifamily supply deliveries of 2024 while positioning for improved fundamentals as new construction slows. The company's management team has exhibited exceptional continuity, with co-founders Campo and Oden leading strategy for over 40 years.

Mi dental means “My dental” in Spanish… And the sound “mi”  relates to “beauty” and “beautiful” in Korean.

Beyond that,
M I are acronyms for minimally invasive – So.. What does that mean? Well, it can be misleading as in terms of understanding as minimal work on teeth? But that’s not what it really means. Mi Dentistry embraces all aspects of the profession as routine procedures with a concept of a “systematic respect for the original natural tooth and tissue”.  It does not suggest that we make small fillings or remove wisdom teeth without symptoms. MI dentistry is the concept of preservation of natural teeth by preventing disease, seizing its progress, removing damaged tissue and replacing it with as little tissue loss as possible. The concept bridges the traditional gap between surgical procedures and preventive care. Mi Dental strives to provide the care that modern dentistry needs today for a healthier smile. Contact us to find out how we can help!

CIM Group is a real estate and infrastructure owner, operator, lender and developer based in Los Angeles. Shaul Kuba, Richard Ressler and Avi Shemesh founded the firm in 1994. In February 2018 it acquired Cole Capital from VEREIT. On June 24, 2026, CIM Real Estate Finance Trust (CMFT), a non-listed REIT managed by CIM affiliates, acquired the real assets management business and investment portfolio of CIM Group, LLC and renamed itself CIM Group, Inc. CIM Group Holdings, a CIM Group, LLC subsidiary, holds 67.5% of the economic and voting interest. Former CMFT shareholders hold the other 32.5%. The company ended its REIT status effective January 1, 2026. Its common stock is quoted over-the-counter under the ticker CMRF, and the company has committed to start pursuing a national exchange listing within 24 months.

CIM reports $31.8 billion in assets owned and operated across five platforms: Real Estate, Credit, Infrastructure, Opportunity Zones and Strategic Opportunities. Its real estate strategies cover core, value-add, net lease and ground-up development. Capital deployed in real estate breaks down as residential at $17.3 billion (37%), office at $11.3 billion (24%), land and horizontal development at $2.3 billion (5%), and industrial at $875 million (2%). The firm also invests in hospitality, retail and mixed-use assets. It lends against office, multifamily, industrial and hospitality properties.

At year-end 2025, the company's own net lease portfolio had 202 properties totaling 6.7 million square feet in 37 states. The largest state exposures by annualized rental income were Virginia (16%), Ohio (12%) and Wisconsin (8%). Four tenants made up 28% of annualized rental income: CVS (9%), Cabela's (7%), United Oil (6%) and Lowe's (6%). Across the wider platform, CIM has invested about $4 billion of equity in the New York metropolitan area since 2010. It also has large projects in Los Angeles, Atlanta and Chicago. The firm has more than 900 employees.

RPM is an Austin, Texas-based multifamily property owner-operator, investment, and development firm active across the United States. Founded in 2002 as Roscoe Property Management by Jason Berkowitz, the company began with just 10 units under management. Through both organic growth and strategic mergers, RPM Living has evolved into one of the nation's largest multifamily operators. 

The firm manages 226,169 units across 26 states. RPM operates through a vertically integrated platform encompassing property management, investment acquisitions, and development. The company maintains 12 regional offices. In 2021, RPM merged with Atlanta-based CF Real Estate Services, expanding its footprint across the Southeast and Midwest. This transaction added approximately 26,000 units to the portfolio. The merger with CF Real Estate Services brought together leadership from both organizations under the RPM brand. 

RPM's assets total a portfolio valued at $3 billion. The company's operations span conventional multifamily, student housing, senior living, and affordable housing sectors. In 2023, RPM Living experienced its largest year of growth, adding 75,000 units to its portfolio and achieving the second-largest portfolio increase among the Top 50 apartment managers.

The NRP Group is a privately held, vertically integrated multifamily real estate firm headquartered in Cleveland, Ohio. J. David Heller and Alan F. Total development investment exceeds $13 billion, including $5 billion allocated to affordable housing.

Western Wealth Communities was founded in 2020 as the in-house property management arm of Western Wealth Capital, a Canadian-based multifamily investment firm. Headquartered in Phoenix, Arizona, the company was created to manage and optimize the growing portfolio of multifamily assets acquired by its parent organization. Since inception, Western Wealth Communities has focused on implementing a disciplined value-creation system that enhances property performance through targeted renovations, operational efficiencies, and community engagement initiatives.

The company’s core business centers on managing Class B multifamily communities in high-growth Sun Belt markets, primarily Arizona, Texas, and Nevada. These regions offer strong fundamentals such as population growth, employment expansion, and favorable business climates, which underpin Western Wealth’s investment thesis. The firm’s strategy emphasizes acquiring properties with significant value-add potential and executing interior and exterior upgrades to drive rent premiums and improve resident experience.

In 1775, our first Navy recruiters were assigned to the Marine Committee, established during the nation’s war for independence.  As the importance of a naval force grew, the Secretary of the Navy assumed direct responsibility for recruiting.  The mission of recruiting was later delegated to the Bureau of Construction and Repair, and then to the Bureau of Navigation, with assignment to the Bureau of Naval Personnel in 1942. 
From 1942 to 1971, the Chief of Naval Personnel remained directly responsible for our Navy’s recruiting mission.  On April 6, 1971, in response to the end of the military draft and an increased emphasis on Navy recruiting, the Secretary of the Navy established the Navy Recruiting Command to serve as a field activity of the Chief of Naval Personnel.  The last draft calls were made in December of the following year. 
Navy Recruiting Command remained in Washington, D.C.,

IBC Bank serves customers across Texas and Oklahoma through a network of main banking and branch facilities, and it also operates branches in shopping malls and supermarkets. The business uses the former name International Bank of Commerce and continues to market its banking services under the IBC Bank brand.

After several years of auditing, their founder Adam Jones noticed a disheartening trend among the nonprofits he worked with: the issues in their accounting systems went unfixed year after year. With this in mind, he started Jones and Associates in 2006 to assist nonprofit organizations with preparation for their financial statement audits. Over a decade later, J & A has grown into a full-service accounting solution, providing a full array of services from bookkeeping to outsourced CFO. The firm has served nonprofits exclusively from Day One, allowing them to focus on their greater mission of making the world a better place.

WORKS Entertainment operates as a full-service music management and event production company with a roster that includes contemporary artists and performance projects.

Asset Living is a third-party property management firm founded in 1986 that serves multifamily, student, and affordable housing communities across the United States. The company also works in active adult and build-to-rent housing, combining property management with services such as compliance training, financial planning, marketing, underwriting, due diligence, construction management, and data analytics. Asset Living operates as a broad real estate management platform that supports owners and institutional partners through property management, asset management, receivership, and investment services. The company maintains a national operating footprint built around residential real estate management and related support functions.

Security Data Supply of Dallas, located in Carrollton, Texas, is a locally owned and operated franchise of a national low-voltage distribution company. Proudly family-owned, veteran-owned, and Texan-owned, the Carrollton branch upholds the company’s commitment to delivering big store products at competitive prices, while maintaining personalized, local service.
Specializing in fire alarms, security systems, access control, audio/video, networking, and home security cameras, Security Data Supply serves contractors and integrators with the right parts, expert support, and fast shipping. Every location is independently managed, ensuring that customers receive knowledgeable service from professionals who understand the industry and the community they serve.

Schools Federal Credit Union is a member-owned, federally chartered credit union that provides banking and financial services to employees of schools, school districts, and affiliated education organizations, as well as their eligible family members. Founded in 1939, the credit union was established to support the financial well-being of education professionals through cooperative, not-for-profit banking. 
Schools FCU offers a full range of consumer financial products and services, including checking and savings accounts, auto and personal loans, credit cards, real estate lending, online and mobile banking, and ATM access. As a federally insured credit union, it operates under the oversight of the National Credit Union Administration (NCUA), with deposits insured up to applicable federal limits.
Headquartered in Torrance, California, Schools Federal Credit Union maintains a small, focused physical footprint with two full-service branch locations in the Los Angeles region. In addition to its own branches, the credit union participates in the CO-OP Shared Branch and ATM network, providing members with access to thousands of shared service locations nationwide while maintaining a localized, member-centric operating model.

Founded in 1990, Statewide Enterprises is a privately held property management firm headquartered in Los Angeles, California. The company specializes in managing multifamily residential properties across Southern California, with a portfolio concentrated in Los Angeles and Ventura Counties. Over the past three decades, Statewide has built a reputation for providing full-service property management solutions to both tenants and property owners.

Statewide’s ownership structure is privately held, with leadership led by President Marc Chopp. The firm operates under a centralized management model, offering services such as rent collection, budgeting, marketing, financial reporting, and maintenance coordination. Its operational philosophy emphasizes transparency, cost control, and long-term asset preservation.

The company’s investment strategy is focused on income-producing residential assets. Statewide targets stabilized or value-add apartment buildings in dense urban neighborhoods, particularly Koreatown, Westlake, Mid-Wilshire, and Hollywood. The firm’s approach includes enhancing operational efficiency and tenant retention through proactive maintenance and on-site personnel supervision.

Statewide Enterprises maintains a full-service maintenance crew available 24/7, which reduces reliance on third-party vendors and improves cost efficiency.

While Statewide's portfolio includes over 1,500 units across more than 30 properties. The firm’s technology infrastructure includes online portals for tenants and owners, supporting digital rent payments, maintenance requests, and financial reporting.

Oak Leaf Management is a fully-integrated commercial real estate services company specializing in management, leasing and brokerage services for residential, commercial, multifamily, office, retail and industrial projects. 

Oak Leaf Management provides residential, multifamily property management services for more than 5000 multifamily units in and around Houston and San Antonio. Oak Leaf also provides commercial property management and leasing services for approximately 1 million SF of commercial office space. 

Additionally, Oak Leaf provides brokerage services for our clients, including due diligence analysis for the acquisition or disposition of multifamily or commercial projects. For more than 40 years, Oak Leaf has served a diverse and demanding client base including financial institutions, private equity groups and individuals as well as foreign investors.

profile.locationBio: Hanover Company is a family-owned real estate developer founded in 1982 and headquartered in Houston, Texas. Since inception, Hanover has developed over $18 billion in total projects, including more than 70,000 multifamily units and 14 million square feet of industrial space. The company maintains in-house capabilities across development, design, construction, property management, capital markets, and legal functions. Hanover's portfolio spans 18 states and 33 cities, with a geographic concentration in Texas and California. California represents the firm's single-largest state exposure with 36 properties, followed by Texas. Hawks Bay is a Los Angeles-based wholesale apparel company specializing in men’s denim jeans and contemporary clothing. Hawks Bay operates primarily as an online wholesale retailer serving fashion businesses and boutiques. Hawks Bay has positioned itself within the apparel and accessories retail sector, focusing on providing streamlined access to wholesale fashion products for its customers.
